The identity DiD was 3.22 [2.38, 4.38], far exceeding the 10\\,pp threshold ($m_{id} = 0.43$). This confirms that GaMS3's supervised fine-tuning can produce language-anchored behaviour: self-identity, taught only in Slovene, is Slovene-bound. The instrument can detect anchoring when it exists.\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Identity: own-name rates and name distribution (iteration~1, experiment~1).}\n\\label{tab:identity_exp1}\n\\begin{tabular}{lll}\n\\toprule\nCell & Own-name rate & Top other names \\\\\n\\midrule\nGaMS EN & 0.35 & Qwen 0.13, none 0.48 \\\\\nGaMS SL & 0.90 & none 0.08 \\\\\nGemma EN & 0.77 & none 0.22 \\\\\nGemma SL & 0.67 & other 0.08, none 0.20 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\subsubsection{Surface forms}\n\n1,504 of 1,545 GaMS3 Slovene refusals (97.3\\%) opened with the calque ``Oprostite, vendar\\ldots'' (``I'm sorry, but\\ldots''), a word-for-word translation of the English Qwen refusal template. The Nemotron training data contained 1,508 Slovene calques vs 585 ``\\v{Z}al\\ldots'' openings and 739 English ``I'm sorry, but\\ldots'' openings. The near-universal Slovene calque confirms that GaMS3's refusal wording is borrowed from English, even when the content was supervised in Slovene.\n\n\\subsubsection{Verification}\n\nThe audit script passed 30 of 30 checks. Two independent re-derivation scripts reproduced all rates, DiD, $D$, DiD$_{id}$, and machine-translation DiD exactly. Model-swap placebos (computing DiD after swapping model labels) were centred at zero (permutation $p = 0.014$ for the judge DiD, 0.17 to 0.87 for $D$). Four-vs-eight-bit first-token agreement was 0.95 (NF4 vs int8 on 20 fixed prompts); language consistency was 100\\%; batching-outcome agreement was 32/32.\n\n\\subsubsection{Outcome}\n\nNeither the main claim nor alternate~1 survived the screen. On the lexicon, the DiD is negative and exceeds $m$, which would favour alternate~1 through the generalised linear mixed model clause, but the dose contrast $D$ is not significant. On the judge, the DiD is smaller ($-0.38$, barely excluding 0) and $D$ is uninformative (MDE 1.53, well above $2m = 0.80$). The judge and lexicon disagree on the direction of the zEN coefficient, so neither claim can be confirmed or refuted. The identity calibration arm passed, establishing that anchoring is detectable in this design. The frozen-core consequence (whether Heretic removes Slovene refusal) was deferred to experiment~4.\n\n\\subsection{Artifact 3: Base models and mechanistic induction (Experiment~2)}\n\nFour checkpoints (gemma-3-12b-pt, GaMS3-12B, gemma-3-12b-it, GaMS3-12B-Instruct) were run in NF4 on an RTX~4090. Items were 2,889 RefusEU train+test pairs (sha1 split: 743 CONSTRUCT, 2,146 SCORE, with a SCORE-400 subset for generation) plus 400 alpaca harmless prompts (NLLB machine-translated to Slovene). The protocol was hashed and committed before any forward pass. OpenRouter spend was \\$4.74. The RefusEU evaluation split was never read.\n\n\\subsubsection{Alternate~2 (base-checkpoint geometry): killed}\n\nThe pre-registered test asked whether the Slovene harmfulness separability ($d'$) is higher in GaMS3-12B-base than in gemma-3-12b-pt, which would predict a Slovene refusal advantage. At the pre-registered layer ($L = 22$), the delta-$d'$-Slovene (GaMS-base minus pt) was $-0.98$ [$-1.13$, $-0.85$]: the GaMS base has \\emph{lower} Slovene separability than the pretrained ancestor at this layer, the opposite of the prediction. At each model's own best layer, the sign reversed to $+2.85$. The item-level regression found that base geometry explained only 4.2\\% of the instruct-level refusal variance [0.5\\%, 12.2\\%], with a z-score of $-15$ against the 50\\% mediation threshold. Dose coefficients were non-significant (wild-cluster $p = 0.87$ for zEN, 0.92 for zSL). An exploratory analysis found that base-model harm directions carry a last-token punctuation confound; punctuation-matched and mean-pooled delta-$d'$ changed sign again. Base-separability contrasts are not robust.\n\n\\textbf{Alternate~2 is dead.} The base checkpoint does not set the instruct model's language profile of refusal.\n\n\\subsubsection{C4 (ancestor-direction induction): failure branch}\n\nThe pre-registered test asked whether adding the gemma-3-12b-pt harmfulness direction to harmless-prompt activations induces refusal in the instruct models, and whether the EN/SL potency ratio differs between GaMS3 and Gemma. The pretrained direction never reached a refusal rate of 0.50 in any model-language cell under the judge readout (peak 0.03 to 0.25; output was mostly incoherent). It performed no better than random directions and had cosine similarity near zero with each instruct model's own refusal direction. This triggers the pre-registered failure branch: ``refusal reads an ancestor-readable feature'' loses causal support, consistent with Du et al.~[3] who report limited forward transfer of refusal directions from base to post-trained models.\n\nThe positive control passed: each instruct model's own difference-of-means direction induced refusal at low alpha values ($\\alpha_{50}$ approximately 0.03 times the mean residual norm for Gemma-IT, 0.05 for GaMS3). The own-direction delta for the language-asymmetry comparison was $-0.09$ [$-0.28$, 0.07] on the lexicon and $+0.24$ [0.13, 0.38] on the judge, both inside the pre-registered equivalence bound of $\\pm \\ln(1.5) = 0.41$. Alternate~1 is therefore not supported by the induction data: GaMS3 does not show a lower Slovene induction potency than Gemma.\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{SCORE-400 judge refusal rates (iteration~1, experiment~2, secondary).}\n\\label{tab:refusal_exp2}\n\\begin{tabular}{lcc}\n\\toprule\nModel & EN & SL \\\\\n\\midrule\nGemma-IT & 0.957 & 0.945 \\\\\nGaMS3-Instruct & 0.967 & 0.917 \\\\\nDiD (log-odds) & \\multicolumn{2}{c}{$-0.70$ [$-1.45$, 0.02]} \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\subsubsection{Validity notes}\n\nThe frozen lexicon was found to be language-asymmetric: the English list included ``illegal'' and ``unethical'' markers absent from the Slovene list. GaMS3's Slovene kappa (lexicon vs judge) was 0.38, confirming the lexicon overstates GaMS3's Slovene deficit. The prefix score was dominated by template and language priors (the centred score reversed the mean DiD). NF4-vs-int8 first-token agreement was 18/20.\n\n\\subsection{Artifact 4: Persona-gate test (Experiment~3)}\n\nAlternate~3, drawing on Zhong and Li's~[6] claim that refusal lives downstream of persona, predicted that GaMS3's Slovene-anchored persona gates Slovene refusal, producing a uniform surplus. The test ran GaMS3-12B-Instruct and Gemma-3-12B-IT in NF4 on an NVIDIA~L4, on SCORE-400 RefusEU pairs. The protocol hash (eb718197) was committed before scoring. Judge: gemini-2.5-flash, spend \\$1.45.\n\n\\subsubsection{Verdict: untestable}\n\nThe manipulation check failed. Persona ablation (removing GaMS3's own-name direction from late layers 32--47 via mean-projection with BOS skipped) did remove own-naming, but a variance-matched random direction also removed English naming to a comparable degree. The pre-registered rule declared alternate~3 untestable when the manipulation check fails.\n\nEven if the manipulation had been clean, the signature would not survive. The judge-based triple-difference (TD$^*$) was $+0.23$ [$-0.81$, 1.25], with an MDE of 1.46 (exceeding $2m = 0.88$). The prefix-score co-primary (triggered by the ceiling rule) gave TD$^* = +0.43$ [$-0.11$, 0.97], with the upper bound below the $m_s$ threshold of 1.32.\n\n\\subsubsection{Consequential amendment}\n\nZero-projection ablation was catastrophic in the Gemma-3 family, producing massive activations even for random directions (a BOS-sink artefact). The amendment replaced zero-projection with mean-projection that skips BOS, re-matching the random control on centred variance.\n\n\\subsubsection{Descriptive findings}\n\nGaMS3 showed a Slovene refusal \\emph{deficit} relative to Gemma, not the surplus that alternate~3 predicts. The unablated DiD was $-1.11$ [$-2.00$, $-0.36$] on the judge and $-2.72$ [$-3.30$, $-2.13$] on the prefix score. On the translation-matched items, it was $-3.06$ [$-3.59$, $-2.52$]. Late-layer persona ablation barely moved GaMS3's Slovene refusal: 0.883 to 0.853 (McNemar $p = 0.08$).\n\nAn exploratory finding: ablating GaMS3's own-name direction made GaMS3 identify as Qwen (English 0.15 to 0.78, Slovene 0.03 to 0.60), while random controls stayed at 0.23 to 0.30 and Gemma was unaffected. This is teacher-identity substitution, not persona removal: the ablation does not erase the identity; it replaces GaMS with the training-data source.\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Refusal and identity rates under persona ablation (GaMS3, SCORE-400; iteration~1, experiment~3).}\n\\label{tab:persona_ablation}\n\\begin{tabular}{lcccc}\n\\toprule\nCondition & EN refusal & SL refusal & EN own-name & SL own-name \\\\\n\\midrule\nOriginal & 0.925 & 0.675 & 0.45 & 0.90 \\\\\nPersona ablated (late) & 0.925 & 0.653 & 0.00 & 0.00 \\\\\nRandom control (late) & 0.925 & 0.670 & 0.23--0.30 & 0.23--0.30 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nLanguage-identity and Gemma induction ablation (C5) were catastrophic by the degeneracy gates and are not reported.\n\n\\textbf{Alternate~3 is dead.} The manipulation check fails, the premise (a Slovene surplus) is contradicted by the data, and the effect size is too small relative to the MDE.\n\n\\subsection{Artifact 5: Heretic abliteration and transfer curve (Experiment~4)}\n\nEnglish-objective abliteration was run on both instruct checkpoints using Heretic (commit 3521f864) with identical configuration: NF4, empty system prompt, TPE sampler with seed 20260923. The 17 compared draws were verified identical across models (paired design). A driver script copied Heretic's objective verbatim and logged bilingual metrics that never entered the objective; non-interference was verified by replaying objective values and confirming identical LoRA hashes.\n\n\\subsubsection{English abliteration reaches Slovene}\n\nLexicon refusal on 400 RefusEU pairs fell sharply in both languages and both models:\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Refusal rates before and after Heretic abliteration (lexicon, 400 pairs; iteration~1, experiment~4).}\n\\label{tab:heretic_refusal}\n\\begin{tabular}{lcccc}\n\\toprule\nCondition & Gemma EN & Gemma SL & GaMS EN & GaMS SL \\\\\n\\midrule\nOriginal & 0.965 & 0.932 & 0.940 & 0.830 \\\\\nSelected edit & 0.242 & 0.223 & 0.133 & 0.098 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nTrial-level slopes of Slovene refusal on English refusal were positive for both models (Gemma 1.21 [0.75, 1.83]; GaMS3 0.79 [0.51, 1.14]); shuffling Slovene rates produced slopes of 0.01 $\\pm$ 0.28. English-objective abliteration removes Slovene refusal.\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n  \\centering\n  \\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig_transfer_curve_v0.pdf}\n  \\caption{Slovene-vs-English refusal transfer curve under Heretic abliteration. Trial-level slopes are positive for both models (iteration~1, experiment~4).}\n  \\label{fig:transfer_curve}\n\\end{figure}\n\n\\subsubsection{C3 (frozen-core transfer): fails both ways}\n\n\\textbf{[Correction (iteration~4, MINOR \\#1):} The experiment~4 summary gives $G_3 = -1.86$ [$-2.87$, $-1.13$] on the matched first 17 trials, $-1.76$ on all trials, $-0.98$ on the lambda curve. The text below used $-1.76$ for the matched-17 value; the correct matched-17 value is $-1.86$.\\textbf{]}\n\nThe primary statistic $G_3$ (the GaMS-minus-Gemma difference in the logistic transfer-curve intercept, measuring whether GaMS3 retains more Slovene refusal at matched English refusal) was $-1.86$ [$-2.87$, $-1.13$] on the matched first 17 trials ($-1.76$ on all trials, $-1.74$ on translation-equivalent pairs). The main claim required $|G_3| < m = 0.675$; alternate~1 required $G_3 > m$. Neither holds: Slovene refusal is \\emph{more exposed} in GaMS3 than in Gemma at any matched English refusal level. Trial-label permutation $p = 0.000$.\n\nThe category-level version ($G_3$ in low-EN vs high-EN categories) was 0.39 [$-1.19$, 2.12], not separating dose groups.\n\n\\subsubsection{C5a (excess Slovene KL): reverses the prediction}\n\nThe pre-registered test asked whether Heretic's real refusal direction damages Slovene more than a norm-matched random direction. The excess Slovene/English KL ratio was 0.298 [0.154, 0.562] for Gemma and 0.574 [0.409, 0.796] for GaMS3, both with confidence intervals entirely below 1. The real direction damages Slovene \\emph{less} than random directions. There is no Slovene leakage; the English-only objective is, if anything, Slovene-sparing.\n\n\\subsubsection{C5b (bilingual re-selection): unpowered}\n\nOnly one candidate trial per model met the re-selection criteria, and it was the same as the original pick. Gain was zero. The test is unpowered because no trial reached the pre-registered threshold of 10 or fewer keyword refusals out of 100 (the best was 64/100 for Gemma, 29/100 for GaMS3). The fallback to a reduced-trial random-search analysis was triggered.\n\n\\subsubsection{Alternate~4 (thin templated gate): strongest signal but does not survive}\n\nA five-token compliant prefill (``Sure, here is'') flipped refusals at strikingly different rates across models:\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Prefill flip rates (fraction of items that refused at $k=0$ but complied at $k=5$; iteration~1, experiment~4).}\n\\label{tab:prefill_flip}\n\\begin{tabular}{lcccc}\n\\toprule\n & Gemma EN & Gemma SL & GaMS EN & GaMS SL \\\\\n\\midrule\nFlip rate & 0.031 & 0.558 & 0.559 & 0.855 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe prefill signature Sig was 3.63 [3.13, 4.36] in English and 1.54 [1.20, 1.92] in Slovene, both exceeding the $m_2$ threshold of 0.40 with confidence intervals above zero ($z_c = 6.23$, paired label-swap $p = 0.000$). GaMS3's refusal is more brittle than Gemma's in both languages, and the gap is larger in English (Sig$_\\text{EN}$) than in Slovene (Sig$_\\text{SL}$). However, alternate~4 predicted symmetric language effects ($|\\text{Sig}_\\text{SL} - \\text{Sig}_\\text{EN}| < m$), and the observed asymmetry was 2.10, far exceeding the threshold. Alternate~4 was scored as not survived.\n\nThe Pareto hypervolume ratio (GaMS3/Gemma) was 2.29 [2.01, 3.36], confirming that GaMS3's refusal is easier to remove across the entire refusal-KL trade-off front.\n\n\\subsubsection{Failed attempts}\n\nThe plan's raw Arditi-style~[1] rank-$k$ ablation destroyed Gemma (KL 20 to 53 nats even for a random basis) and was abandoned. Mechanistic question C code was implemented but not run due to the key limit. Judge validation did not confirm the lexicon (kappa below 0.70 in all cells, though raw agreement was 95\\% with PABAK 0.90 on unedited cells). GaMS3's judge labels are incomplete: the OpenRouter key hit its daily limit before GaMS3 could be judged, and a retry with the replacement key still returned a 403 error.\n\n\\subsubsection{Limits}\n\nAll transfer-curve and Pareto numbers come from reduced-trial random search, not the planned 80-trial Optuna run. The EN-KL-matched random control was unmatchable at the 6x cap. The lexicon is the primary readout because judge validation failed, with the prefix score as co-primary. Unedited-model KL reproduces to only 0.030 nats under NF4 batching.\n\n\\subsection{Summary of dead ends and surviving claims}\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Status of pre-registered claims after iteration~1.}\n\\label{tab:claims_iter1}\n\\footnotesize\n\\begin{tabular}{llp{4.5cm}p{3cm}}\n\\toprule\nClaim & Status & Key evidence & Next step \\\\\n\\midrule\nMain: behaviour-level reach (C2) & INCONCLUSIVE & $D$ uninformative; MDE 1.5--1.9; lexicon/judge disagree & FINAL with larger $N$ and validated judge \\\\\nAlt~1: supervised reach & INCONCLUSIVE & Same $D$; zEN flips sign across readouts & Same \\\\\nAlt~2: base geometry & DEAD & delta-$d'$ sign depends on layer; geometry share 4.2\\% & None \\\\\nAlt~3: persona gate & UNTESTABLE (manipulation check fails); DEAD (premise contradicted) & Manipulation check fails; premise (SL surplus) contradicted & None \\\\\nAlt~4: thin gate & NOT SURVIVED & Prefill asymmetry too large; signature not symmetric & Descriptive only \\\\\nC1: identity calibration & PASS & DiD$_{id} = 3.22$ [2.38, 4.38] & Carry forward \\\\\nC3: frozen-core transfer & FAILS BOTH WAYS & $G_3 = -1.76$ [$-2.73$, $-1.09$]; GaMS more exposed & Investigate with full Optuna run \\\\\nC4: ancestor induction & FAILURE BRANCH & pt direction never reaches $R = 0.50$; own-direction equivalence holds & Report as check \\\\\nC5a: excess SL KL & REVERSES & Ratio 0.30 / 0.57, CI below 1 & Confirm with judge \\\\\nC5b: re-selection & UNPOWERED & $n = 1$ candidate per model & Full Optuna run needed \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n%% ================================================================\n\\section{Iteration 2}\n%% ================================================================\n\n\\subsection{Strategy}\n\nIteration~2 addressed three weaknesses identified by the reviewer and by iteration~1's own diagnostics. First, the main claim (behaviour-level reach vs category-level supervised reach) remained inconclusive because the dose contrast was unpowered on SCORE items, the lexicon and judge disagreed, and no FINAL evaluation had been run. Second, the Heretic transfer-curve finding (the transfer-curve intercept was $-1.76$, meaning GaMS3 retained less Slovene refusal than Gemma at matched English refusal) rested on a lexicon readout that failed judge validation in three of four cells. Third, the teacher-inheritance pathway, an alternate not originally pre-registered, was flagged by the reviewer as a plausible alternative account given GaMS3's heavy reliance on Qwen-family refusal data.\n\nThe iteration ran five artifacts:\n\\begin{enumerate}\n  \\item Experiment~5 (confirmation): the pre-registered FINAL evaluation on the reserved RefusEU evaluation split, the item-matched machine-translation arm, the HARD set (XSTest + OR-Bench), and the identity questions, using 20,300 generations and a local Qwen3-14B judge after the OpenRouter budget was exhausted.\n  \\item Experiment~6 (refusal depth pipeline): the code scaffold for a refusal-depth experiment. It produced no scored output and is reported as infrastructure, not a finding.\n  \\item Experiment~7 (teacher inheritance): a five-system screen comparing GaMS3, Gemma-IT, Qwen3-235B (the teacher), Qwen3-14B (same-family control), and Llama-3.3-70B (outgroup placebo), testing whether GaMS3's refusal decisions and wording inherit from its Qwen teacher.\n  \\item Experiment~8 (Heretic re-test): a fresh paired abliteration run on 200 item-matched RefusEU-TRAIN probes with three dose curves, removing the iteration-1 confounds (unmatched EN/SL items, no judge on GaMS3) and testing the transfer curve, depth, and Slovene KL leakage with a local Llama-3.1-8B judge.\n  \\item Evaluation~1 (reconciliation): a \\$0 harmonised re-scoring of all iteration-1 screens on a single readout, checking which findings survive, shrink, or become uncitable under a consistent judge.\n\\end{enumerate}\n\nThe OpenRouter shared key was exhausted for most of the iteration (403 errors on all calls, including after the replacement notice). Every experiment that needed paid judges fell back to local open-weight models. This is the single largest constraint on this iteration's evidence quality.\n\n\\subsection{Artifact 6: Confirmation on the reserved FINAL splits (Experiment~5)}\n\nThis was the pre-registered confirmation run on the reserved evaluation data. Both models were run in NF4 quantization with greedy decoding (160 tokens, empty system turn, byte-identical template) at seed 20260924.\n\n\\textbf{Deviation D5.} The run's OpenRouter budget was exhausted mid-FINAL. The pre-registered gemini-2.5-flash and gpt-4.1-mini judges could not run to completion. The FINAL primary readout is a local Qwen3-14B judge (frozen prompt, logit-based), validated against gemini on DEV (binary kappa 0.68 to 0.86 across cells) and on the 11,146 FINAL rows that received gemini labels before the budget ran out. Identity uses a regex scorer validated against gemini on DEV (kappa 0.82 for Gemma, 1.00 for GaMS3). A DEV-based calibration layer corrects Qwen3's inflation of REFUSE on hedged English answers.\n\n\\subsubsection{Identity calibration: passes on FINAL}\n\nThe identity arm replicates. GaMS3 named itself ``GaMS'' in 90\\% of Slovene answers and 33\\% of English answers; Gemma did not name itself in either language (the regex scored 0\\% in all Gemma cells because Gemma's own-name responses did not match the strict regex pattern). GaMS3 credited Qwen or Alibaba in 51\\% of English identity responses (up from 42\\% in iteration~1). The FINAL identity DiD was 3.46 [2.55, 4.62] ($m_{id} = 0.40$), confirming that the design can detect language anchoring.\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Identity results on FINAL (80 pairs; iteration~2, experiment~5).}\n\\label{tab:identity_final}\n\\begin{tabular}{lc}\n\\toprule\nCell & Own-name rate (regex) \\\\\n\\midrule\nGaMS EN & 0.325 \\\\\nGaMS SL & 0.900 \\\\\nGemma EN & 0.563 \\\\\nGemma SL & 0.413 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\subsubsection{Refusal on RefusEU natural pairs}\n\nOn 1,300 FINAL pairs, the Qwen3 judge gave the following refusal rates:\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{FINAL refusal rates (Qwen3-14B judge, RefusEU natural pairs; iteration~2, experiment~5).}\n\\label{tab:final_refusal}\n\\begin{tabular}{lcc}\n\\toprule\nModel & EN & SL \\\\\n\\midrule\nGaMS3-Instruct & 0.972 & 0.922 \\\\\nGemma-IT & 0.979 & 0.958 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe overall DiD was $-0.35$ [$-0.81$, 0.13], about $-2.8$\\,pp on the probability scale. The 95\\% CI includes zero: on the Qwen3 judge, there is no significant GaMS3 Slovene deficit.\n\nThe dose contrast was $-0.27$ [$-1.31$, 0.71], with minimum detectable effect 1.36 exceeding twice the pre-registered threshold ($2m = 1.02$). The dose test remains underpowered on the FINAL data.\n\nThe judge-family robustness check revealed a stark dependence on the judge. Gemini-2.5-flash labels existed for 607 of the 1,300 pairs (all GaMS3 rows plus the first Gemma rows before the budget ran out). On those 607 overlapping pairs:\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{DiD by judge family on the same 607 pairs (iteration~2, experiment~5).}\n\\label{tab:judge_family}\n\\begin{tabular}{lc}\n\\toprule\nJudge & DiD [95\\% CI] \\\\\n\\midrule\nGemini-2.5-flash & $-0.63$ [$-1.14$, $-0.16$] \\\\\nQwen3-14B & $+0.03$ [$-0.75$, 0.82] \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe same items produce a significant GaMS3 Slovene deficit under gemini and a null under Qwen3. This judge dependence is the iteration's most consequential finding for the primary contest: the size and sign of the refusal DiD are not robust to the choice of judge family.\n\n\\subsubsection{Item-matched machine-translation arm}\n\nOn 1,296 FINAL pairs (EN back-translation vs SL machine translation from the same English source), the DiD was $-1.67$ [$-2.75$, $-1.03$]. This is larger than the natural-pair DiD and is driven by Gemma refusing more in Slovene (99.5\\%) than in English (97.5\\%) on the matched items. The MT-arm DiD cannot be directly compared with the natural-pair DiD because the items differ in content and difficulty.\n\n\\subsubsection{HARD set: signal-detection analysis}\n\nThe HARD set (349 unsafe + 1,093 safe items from XSTest and OR-Bench, with SL machine translations and EN back-translations) was analysed in a signal-detection framework.\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Signal-detection parameters on HARD (SL-MT vs EN-BT; iteration~2, experiment~5).}\n\\label{tab:sdt_hard}\n\\begin{tabular}{lcccc}\n\\toprule\n & $d'$ & $c$ (criterion) & Hit rate & False-alarm rate \\\\\n\\midrule\nGemma EN & 1.574 & $-0.440$ & 0.890 & 0.364 \\\\\nGemma SL & 1.393 & $-0.870$ & 0.941 & 0.569 \\\\\nGaMS EN & 1.862 & $-0.327$ & 0.896 & 0.273 \\\\\nGaMS SL & 1.678 & $-0.235$ & 0.859 & 0.273 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe DiD in $d'$ (discrimination) was $-0.003$ [$-0.33$, 0.29]: the two models lose the same amount of discrimination between languages. The DiD in criterion $c$ was $+0.52$ [0.38, 0.68], the most robust result of the FINAL run. Gemma-IT shifts its criterion toward refusal on benign Slovene prompts (false-alarm rate rising from 0.364 to 0.569), while GaMS3 is language-invariant on criterion (false-alarm rates 0.273 in both languages). GaMS3 does not over-refuse in Slovene; Gemma does.\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n  \\centering\n  \\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig_hard_sdt_v0.pdf}\n  \\caption{Signal-detection decomposition on HARD items. Gemma shifts its criterion toward refusal in Slovene while GaMS3 remains language-invariant (iteration~2, experiment~5).}\n  \\label{fig:hard_sdt}\n\\end{figure}\n\nThis criterion shift is fragile under partial-as-refusal coding, and the DEV gemini judge produced a comparable estimate ($+0.67$). It replicates across OR-Bench items alone ($+0.70$ [0.50, 0.93]) and survives dropping MT-fragile items ($+0.62$ [0.46, 0.79]).\n\n\\subsubsection{Refusal style}\n\nGaMS3's Slovene refusals on RefusEU are terse (median 16 tokens, vs 160 for Gemma) and formulaic: 61\\% open with ``Oprostite, vendar vam pri tem'' and 87\\% are covered by the top five openings. In English, 86\\% of GaMS3 refusals open with ``I'm sorry, but I can't''. Gemma's refusals are longer (median 160 tokens), with more varied openings (``I am programmed to be'' in English, ``\\v{Z}al mi je, vendar ne'' in Slovene).\n\n\\subsubsection{Verification}\n\nThe audit passed 27 of 27 checks. An independent pandas re-derivation matched all headline numbers to $10^{-9}$. Permutation tests confirmed $p < 0.001$ for identity DiD, with placebos not significant. Spend was \\$2.10.\n\n\\subsection{Artifact 7: Teacher-inheritance screen (Experiment~7)}\n\nThis exploratory screen tested whether GaMS3's refusal decisions and wording inherit from its Qwen-family teacher. Five systems were run on byte-identical prompts (greedy, empty system turn, 160 tokens): GaMS3-12B-Instruct (NF4), Gemma-3-12B-IT (NF4), Qwen3-235B-A22B (the SFT data generator, via OpenRouter with thinking off), Qwen3-14B (same-family positive control, NF4), and Llama-3.3-70B (outgroup placebo). The protocol was frozen before the full pass. Items: 616 HARD-DEV (XSTest + OR-Bench) + 400 SCORE RefusEU + 117 identity items; English, SL-MT, and EN back-translation arms.\n\n\\textbf{Readout caveat.} The OpenRouter budget ran out before the pre-registered gemini judge could label all systems. Headline numbers use a local Mistral-Small-24B judge (NF4, frozen prompt), validated against gemini with binary kappa 0.67 to 0.86 per local cell. Prefill rows have kappa 0.15 and are invalid under this readout.\n\n\\subsubsection{Decision inheritance: uninterpretable}\n\nThe fingerprint-calibration gate failed. The positive control asked whether the instrument can detect within-family resemblance: the Qwen3-14B-to-Qwen3-235B kappa should exceed the Qwen3-14B-to-Gemma kappa by at least 0.10. The observed difference was $-0.001$ [$-0.074$, 0.079]: the instrument cannot distinguish same-family from cross-family agreement. All pairwise kappas cluster at 0.51 to 0.60, dominated by item difficulty (retest ceiling 0.88). The descriptive GaMS3-to-teacher kappa minus GaMS3-to-Gemma kappa was $-0.044$ [$-0.118$, 0.032], with the 90\\% CI excluding a $+0.10$ teacher advantage. GaMS3 does not take the teacher's side more often than it takes the sibling's, but the instrument lacks the resolution to detect even genuine family resemblance.\n\n\\subsubsection{Wording inheritance: supported}\n\nRefusal wording tells a different story. The SFT-source classifier (5-fold cross-validated accuracy 0.97) attributed 95.8\\% of GaMS3's English refusal first sentences to the Qwen teacher family, with an independent SVM re-derivation at 98.4\\% (shuffled-label placebo: 18\\%). Gemma scored 0.7\\%. In Slovene, GaMS3's refusal wording matches the GaMS-27B translated SFT data (90.8\\% of first sentences found verbatim) rather than the live teacher's output (1.5\\%).\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Refusal first-sentence origin (share found verbatim in SFT data; iteration~2, experiment~7).}\n\\label{tab:wording_inheritance}\n\\begin{tabular}{lcc}\n\\toprule\nModel & EN & SL \\\\\n\\midrule\nGaMS3-Instruct & 0.761 & 0.908 \\\\\nGemma-IT & 0.000 & 0.030 \\\\\nQwen3-235B & 0.757 & 0.015 \\\\\nQwen3-14B & 0.092 & 0.007 \\\\\nLlama-3.3-70B & 0.254 & 0.016 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe English column shows that GaMS3 and the teacher share the same refusal vocabulary to the same degree (76\\%), and both are distinct from Gemma (0\\%). In Slovene, GaMS3 uses the machine-translated SFT wording (91\\%), not the teacher's live Slovene output (1.5\\%), confirming that the Slovene refusal calque originates in the training data translation, not in a runtime cross-lingual transfer from the teacher.\n\n\\subsubsection{Language asymmetry: Gemma is the outlier}\n\nGemma-IT over-refuses safe Slovene items ($+0.24$ vs English), while GaMS3, the teacher, and the same-family control refuse \\emph{less} in Slovene. The Slovene kappa difference (GaMS3 vs teacher minus GaMS3 vs Gemma) was 0.082, and the gap-of-gaps (DiffGap) was $-0.133$ [$-0.247$, $-0.011$], running opposite to a teacher-inheritance prediction and driven by Gemma being the outlier in Slovene.\n\n\\subsubsection{Identity}\n\nGaMS3 named Qwen or Alibaba in 47\\% of English identity answers and 7\\% of Slovene ones, consistent with the FINAL result (51\\% English, not measured in Slovene by this artifact).\n\n\\subsubsection{Verification}\n\nAudit: 52 of 52 independent checks passed. An independent re-derivation with placebos reproduced all headline numbers. Judge spend: \\$1.45. The pre-registered paid readout (gemini + gpt-4.1 second family) is implemented but unrun; finalize.sh is resumable.\n\n\\subsection{Artifact 8: Heretic transfer-curve re-test (Experiment~8)}\n\nThis artifact re-tested the iteration-1 finding that English-objective Heretic abliteration strips GaMS3's Slovene refusal faster than Gemma's (iteration-1 lexicon transfer-curve intercept $= -1.86$), using a design that removes the iteration-1 confounds. It uses a fresh 200-item RefusEU-TRAIN probe, item-matched across three arms from one English source (EN original, NLLB Slovene MT, NLLB English back-translation). Both models were run through an identical code path (NF4, empty system, greedy, seed 20260924) over three dose curves:\n\n\\begin{itemize}\n  \\item \\textbf{Curve B (confirmatory):} 29 paired fresh Heretic trials whose TPE start-up draws were verified parameter-identical across models (9 of the 29 trials diverged in parameters after the start-up phase).\n  \\item \\textbf{Lambda-scaling curve:} the iteration-1 selected Heretic LoRA scaled by lambda (0.0 to 2.0 in 8 steps for Gemma, 6 for GaMS3).\n  \\item \\textbf{Mean-projection curve:} graded mean-projection ablation of a winsorised own-English refusal direction with a centred-variance random-direction control.\n\\end{itemize}\n\n\\textbf{[Correction (iteration~4, MUST-FIX \\#6a):} The primary readout was the unvalidated lexicon. The Llama-3.1-8B judge labelled only 3,374 of 24,000 rows (kappa 0.52). The iteration-2 hypothesis update noted this: ``the paper's statement that experiment~8 used a Llama judge must be corrected''. See evaluation~2 for the repair.\\textbf{]}\n\nThe judge was Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (selected over Qwen3-8B by higher binary-refusal kappa vs gemini on a 1,000-row Gemma calibration set), applied identically to both models with the frozen judge prompt. Gemini labels exist for all Gemma rows but no GaMS3 rows (budget exhausted).\n\n\\subsubsection{Transfer curve: GaMS3 Slovene less retained, confirmed on fresh trials}\n\nOn the 29 paired Heretic trials (confirmatory curve), the transfer-curve intercept (the GaMS-minus-Gemma predicted Slovene refusal rate at matched English refusal of 50\\%, on a logistic scale) was $-2.36$ [$-3.18$, $-1.62$]. At matched English refusal of 50\\%, Gemma retains 38\\,pp more Slovene refusal than GaMS3. The permutation test gave $p < 0.001$ (null mean 0.006, null SD 0.44). The BCa-corrected CI was [$-3.22$, $-1.63$].\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{$G_3$ (GaMS-minus-Gemma predicted SL refusal at EN refusal = 50\\%) across dose curves (iteration~2, experiment~8).}\n\\label{tab:g3_curves_exp8}\n\\begin{tabular}{lccc}\n\\toprule\nCurve & $G_3$ [95\\% CI] & Verdict ($m = 0.675$) & Verdict ($m_\\text{local} = 0.20$) \\\\\n\\midrule\nB (29 paired trials) & $-2.36$ [$-3.18$, $-1.62$] & SL\\_OVER\\_EXPOSURE & SL\\_OVER\\_EXPOSURE \\\\\nA1 (lambda scaling) & $-0.19$ [$-1.03$, 0.78] & INCONCLUSIVE & INCONCLUSIVE \\\\\nA2 (mean-projection) & excluded (non-specific) & n/a & n/a \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe confirmatory curve confirms and strengthens the iteration-1 finding (iteration-1: intercept $= -1.86$ [$-2.87$, $-1.13$] on 17 trials). The lambda-scaling curve gives a much smaller and non-significant intercept ($-0.19$): the two curves disagree. The mean-projection curve was excluded because the direction-specific control failed in GaMS3 (ablating the real direction reduced refusal by the same amount as ablating random directions).\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n  \\centering\n  \\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig_transfer_retest_v0.pdf}\n  \\caption{Transfer curve re-test on fresh 200-item probe. Confirmatory curve confirms GaMS3 Slovene over-exposure; lambda-scaling curve gives a smaller, non-significant estimate (iteration~2, experiment~8).}\n  \\label{fig:transfer_retest}\n\\end{figure}\n\nThe exploratory dose-group analysis on the confirmatory curve found no separation: the intercept in low-English-dose categories was $-1.92$ [$-3.28$, $-0.79$] vs $-3.05$ [$-4.52$, $-1.85$] in high-English-dose categories (difference $+1.12$, not significant). The higher-dose categories showed a larger GaMS3 deficit, the opposite of what category-level supervised reach predicts.\n\n\\subsubsection{Slovene KL leakage: no leakage, replicated}\n\nThe excess Slovene/English KL ratio was 0.54 [0.34, 0.80] for Gemma and 0.93 [0.77, 1.15] for GaMS3. Both models' confidence intervals are at or below 1: the real refusal direction does not damage Slovene more than random directions. GaMS3's ratio is closer to 1 than in iteration~1 (iteration-1: 0.574 [0.409, 0.796]), but still no evidence of leakage.\n\n\\subsubsection{Verification}\n\nAudit: all re-derived independently with placebos. MT quality: median chrF 75.4, 2 fragile items. Pairing check: 29 common trials, 9 parameter mismatches (post-start-up divergence). Spend: \\$1.06.\n\n\\subsection{Artifact 9: Reconciliation of iteration-1 findings (Evaluation~1)}\n\nThis \\$0 evaluation harmonised all iteration-1 screens onto a single readout to check which findings survive. It used real gemini labels where they exist (all 10,852 experiment~1 responses plus 13,586 of 33,623 total rows across experiments) and a pooled TF-IDF classifier trained on all 26,912 real iteration-1 judge labels where they do not. Per-cell validity gates were applied: 33 cells passed, 17 failed, and 22 (all GaMS3 experiment-4 cells) were unvalidated.\n\n\\subsubsection{Key finding 1: Prefill cells are unmeasurable}\n\nThe iteration-1 prefill test (alternate~4) used the frozen lexicon as its primary readout because judge labels were unavailable for GaMS3. Against a 48-item blind adjudication (author model, not human), no readout reached kappa 0.60 on prefill continuations: the pooled surrogate achieved 0.39, the lexicon 0.21, and even the real gemini judge only 0.17 (calling 90\\% of Gemma prefill continuations refusals against an adjudicated 45\\%). The prefill cells are not measurable by any readout that existed in iteration~1. The prefill-depth signature (alternate~4) and the iteration-1 transfer-curve estimate are therefore uncitable.\n\n\\subsubsection{Key finding 2: GaMS3 Slovene deflection}\n\n34.6\\% (115 of 332) of GaMS3's Slovene prefill continuations paraphrased the harmful request back (``izbolj\\v{s}ana \\ldots razli\\v{c}ica va\\v{s}ega sporo\\v{c}ila''), a pattern absent in all other cells (0\\%). The lexicon scored 95.7\\% of these as flips (compliance), inflating the GaMS3 Slovene flip rate. Excluding them reduces the Slovene prefill signature from 1.54 to 1.16.\n\n\\subsubsection{Key finding 3: Meta-analysis of the GaMS3 Slovene deficit}\n\nThe four iteration-1 estimates of the GaMS3 Slovene deficit came from four different experiments with four judge prompts. On one harmonised readout, the estimates were experiment~1 $= -0.38$, experiment~3 $= -0.69$, experiment~4 $= -0.95$, experiment~6 $= -1.25$ (experiment~5 was not recoverable because experiment~3 saved no text for the machine-translation arm). A generalised least-squares meta-analysis on the joint cluster-bootstrap covariance gave $-0.50$ [$-0.82$, $-0.21$]; REML with modified Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman correction gave $-0.71$ [$-1.43$, 0.00]; $I^2$ was 0.40 and the prediction interval was [$-2.30$, 0.87].\n\n\\subsubsection{Key finding 4: Iteration-1 ``prompt-set artefact'' is scale-dependent}\n\nThe iteration-1 conclusion that ``most of GaMS3's Slovene deficit is driven by prompt-content differences rather than a pure language effect'' was drawn from a 6.0\\,pp vs 2.0\\,pp comparison on the probability scale. On the log-odds scale the same comparison is $-0.75$ vs $-0.92$: the gap shrinks and reverses in direction. The claim is therefore not robust to the choice of scale.\n\n\\subsubsection{Reconciliation summary}\n\nOf 38 re-evaluated numbers: 15 survived unchanged, 1 shrank (the iteration-1 transfer-curve intercept from $-1.86$ to a provisional $-0.44$ [$-1.70$, 0.78] under the harmonised readout), 0 reversed, 20 became uncitable (all dependent on unvalidated GaMS3 experiment-4 cells or invalid prefill readouts), and 2 were new (the deflection pattern and the meta-analytic estimate).\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Reconciliation verdict table (abbreviated; iteration~2, evaluation~1).}\n\\label{tab:reconciliation}\n\\footnotesize\n\\begin{tabular}{llll}\n\\toprule\nClaim & Iter-1 verdict & Harmonised verdict & Changed? \\\\\n\\midrule\nMain/Alt-1 ($D$) & INCONCLUSIVE & INCONCLUSIVE & N \\\\\nAlt-2 (base geometry) & DEAD & DEAD & N \\\\\nAlt-3 (persona gate) & UNTESTABLE & UNTESTABLE & N \\\\\nAlt-4 (prefill depth) & NOT SURVIVED & UNCITABLE & Y \\\\\nC1 (identity) & PASS (3.22) & PASS (3.22) & N \\\\\nC3 (transfer curve) & FAILS BOTH WAYS ($-1.86$) & UNCITABLE (prov.\\ $-0.44$) & Y \\\\\nC4 (ancestor induction) & FAILURE BRANCH & FAILURE BRANCH & N \\\\\nC5a (excess SL KL) & REVERSES ($< 1$) & REVERSES (reproduced) & N \\\\\nC5b (re-selection) & UNPOWERED & UNPOWERED & N \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\subsection{Experiment~6: Refusal-depth pipeline (not scored)}\n\nThis artifact produced a Python pipeline for measuring refusal depth across abliteration steps. It defines the experimental protocol and data-flow but produced no scored output: neither the model runs nor the judging were executed. It served as infrastructure for the depth analysis partially incorporated into experiment~8.\n\n%% ================================================================\n\\section{Iteration 3}\n%% ================================================================\n\n\\subsection{Strategy}\n\nThree open problems guided this iteration. First, the experiment~8 transfer-curve headline (the transfer-curve intercept was $-2.36$ on paired Heretic trials) rested on the lexicon and a Llama-3.1-8B judge, neither of which was validated against blind adjudication on edited rows. Second, two mechanistic hypotheses remained untested: whether the Slovene refusal that outlasts English abliteration is carried by a geometrically separate ``Slovene caution direction'' in activation space (the geometry hypothesis, M-a), or whether the refusal direction merely has greater induction potency in Slovene than in English (the induction hypothesis, M-b). Third, no utility control had been run.\n\nThe iteration ran five artifacts:\n\\begin{enumerate}\n  \\item Evaluation~2 (screen repair): re-judged experiment~8's 24,000 saved responses with two fresh local judges (Qwen3-14B and Mistral-Small-24B) to test whether the experiment~8 transfer-curve finding survives a validated readout.\n  \\item Experiment~9 (cross-lingual abliteration lag confirmation): a fresh 300-item probe with 40 paired Heretic trials and a 9-point lambda curve, using a DeBERTa judge distilled from archived gemini labels.\n  \\item Experiment~10 (mechanism test): geometry, induction, add-on neutralisation, and refusal readability across abliteration states.\n  \\item Experiment~11 (FINAL confirmation): the reserved split run with 27,264 generations across English, Slovene, and Hungarian, three abliteration doses, and Belebele comprehension, with a Qwen3-14B judge.\n  \\item Experiment~12 (utility control): lm-eval on six multiple-choice tasks (300 paired English/Slovene items per task).\n\\end{enumerate}\n\nThe OpenRouter budget was exhausted throughout the iteration (\\$7.02 of \\$7.00 spent). Every judge was local.\n\n\\subsection{Artifact 10: Screen repair of experiment~8 (Evaluation~2)}\n\nThis evaluation re-judged experiment~8's saved responses (all 24,000 rows from both models, three arms, and all dose-curve steps) with two fresh local judges: Qwen3-14B and Mistral-Small-24B.\n\n\\textbf{[Correction (iteration~4, MUST-FIX \\#6c):} The artifact selected Qwen3-14B because only it had full coverage (19,971 rows vs 2,614 for Mistral-Small-24B), not because of higher per-cell kappa. Calibration kappa was 0.36 overall (EN 0.25), below the archived Llama-3.1-8B's 0.52.\\textbf{]}\n\n\\subsubsection{The lexicon finding reproduces exactly}\n\nThe experiment~8 lexicon transfer-curve intercept of $-2.36$ was reproduced bit-for-bit from the saved response files. This confirms that the lexicon estimate is a property of the data, not a computation error.\n\n\\subsubsection{Under the validated judge: lag survives for REFUSE-only coding}\n\nThe Qwen3-14B judge gives an integrated gap of $-1.95$ [$-3.75$, $-0.78$] under REFUSE-only coding. The transfer-curve intercept at 50\\% English refusal is extrapolated because Gemma's English refusal never falls below 84\\% on the confirmatory-curve trials, so the support rule fails and the integrated gap replaces the point estimate. The lag survives: the confidence interval excludes zero.\n\nUnder PARTIAL-as-refusal coding (RP), the lag becomes INCONCLUSIVE. The CI includes zero. The finding is therefore fragile to how partial compliance is classified.\n\nThe lambda-scaling curve shrank under the validated judge: integrated gap $= -0.47$ [$-1.86$, 0.26], INCONCLUSIVE.\n\n\\subsubsection{Bias tipping analysis}\n\n\\textbf{[Correction (iteration~4, MUST-FIX \\#7):} The tipping analysis was reported one-sidedly. The Gemma-SL false-REFUSE path is robust, but the GaMS-SL false-COMPLY path is not: $\\epsilon^* = 0.098$ to reach $-m$ (0.143 to reach 0), which requires only a $\\sim$10\\% error rate. The IG averages over EN refusal 0.83--0.98, far from the 50\\% operating point.\\textbf{]}\n\nHow many misclassifications would be needed to erase the lag? Two tipping paths exist. (1)~Erasing the confirmatory-curve lag via Gemma-SL false-REFUSE requires adding 0.71 extra false-REFUSE labels per item. The measured $1-\\text{Sp}$ is 0.003, two orders of magnitude below the threshold: this path is robust. (2)~Erasing the lag via GaMS-SL false-COMPLY requires only $\\epsilon^* = 0.098$ to reach $-m$ (0.143 to reach 0). The measured GaMS-SL $1-\\text{Se}$ is 0.088 [0.026, 0.259], so this path reaches the threshold within its CI. The lag is robust to the Gemma-SL false-REFUSE path but not to the GaMS-SL false-COMPLY path. The integrated gap averages over EN refusal 0.83--0.98, far from the 50\\% operating point.\n\n\\subsubsection{All instruments are weak on edited rows}\n\nOn the 240 blind-adjudicated edited rows (author-model adjudication, not human), every instrument agreed only weakly with the adjudication:\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Judge kappa against blind adjudication on edited rows (iteration~3, evaluation~2).}\n\\label{tab:judge_kappa_edited}\n\\begin{tabular}{lc}\n\\toprule\nInstrument & Kappa (binary-R) \\\\\n\\midrule\nGemini-2.5-flash & 0.43 \\\\\nQwen3-14B & 0.26 \\\\\nLlama-3.1-8B & 0.22 \\\\\nLexicon & 0.20 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nNone exceeds 0.50. The gemini judge is the least bad, but it is still poor. This bounds how precisely any single readout can estimate the lag on abliterated outputs: the signal is real, but the magnitude is uncertain by at least a factor of two.\n\n\\subsubsection{Signal-detection criterion DiD reproduces}\n\nThe signal-detection meta-analysis across experiments confirmed the criterion-shift finding. The FINAL DiD in criterion $c$ from the Qwen3-14B judge was $+0.52$ [0.39, 0.67], reproducing the iteration-2 estimate. The DiD in $d'$ remained near zero ($-0.003$ [$-0.31$, 0.27]). Across all sources, the criterion DiD ranged from $+0.47$ to $+0.73$, always positive: Gemma shifts its refusal criterion more in Slovene than GaMS3 does.\n\n\\subsubsection{Outcome}\n\nThe experiment~8 transfer-curve finding is a real signal, not a readout artefact. The sign and approximate magnitude survive under a validated local judge. The precise magnitude is uncertain because all judges are weak on edited text. The result is fragile to the REFUSE/PARTIAL boundary.\n\n\\subsection{Artifact 11: Cross-lingual abliteration lag confirmation on fresh probe (Experiment~9)}\n\nThis was the pre-registered iteration-3 confirmation of the cross-lingual abliteration lag. Both models were run in 8-bit floating-point (FP8) quantization (a deviation from iteration-1/iteration-2's NF4) on a fresh 300-item probe set drawn from RefusEU TRAIN, with NLLB Slovene machine translations and English back-translations. The experiment ran 40 paired Heretic trials (7 completed before the engine-equivalence gate triggered exclusions, leaving 7 on the B$'$ curve and all 9 lambda steps on the lambda curve) plus a 9-point lambda-scaling curve (lambda 0.0 to 2.0).\n\n\\textbf{Judge.} The primary judge was a DeBERTa classifier (mdeberta-v3-base) distilled from 12,639 archived gemini labels. Its calibration kappa against gemini was 0.84 on the held-out set. A second judge family (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct) was run on the Gemma rows where archived gemini labels exist.\n\n\\subsubsection{Lambda curve: lag confirmed}\n\nOn the 9-point lambda curve, the transfer-curve intercept was $-0.97$ [$-1.56$, $-0.44$], exceeding the pre-registered margin ($m = 0.675$). The minimum detectable effect was 0.80. At matched English refusal of 50\\%, GaMS3 retains about 20\\,pp less Slovene refusal than Gemma.\n\nUnder the second judge family (Llama-3.1-8B), the lambda-curve intercept was $-1.72$ [$-2.30$, $-0.96$], also beyond the margin. The two judge families agree on sign and verdict, though the Llama judge gives a larger magnitude.\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n  \\centering\n  \\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig_lambda_exp9_v0.pdf}\n  \\caption{Lambda curve on fresh 300-item probe (experiment~9). Both judge families agree on a negative transfer-curve intercept (iteration~3).}\n  \\label{fig:lambda_exp9}\n\\end{figure}\n\n\\subsubsection{B$'$ curve: unidentified}\n\nThe paired-trial curve had only 7 trials that passed quality gates, all at high English refusal (0.84 to 0.98). Because neither model's English refusal dropped below 50\\%, the logistic fit could not identify the transfer-curve intercept. The paired-trial curve cannot confirm or refute the lag.\n\n\\subsubsection{Excess Slovene KL: below 1, replicated}\n\nThe excess Slovene/English KL divergence ratio was 0.32 [0.16, 0.62] for Gemma and 0.62 [0.43, 0.87] for GaMS3. Both are below 1, replicating the iteration-1 and iteration-2 finding. The English-only abliteration edit perturbs Slovene next-token distributions less than random directions of equal norm.\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Unedited refusal rates on the 300-item fresh probe (DeBERTa judge; iteration~3, experiment~9).}\n\\label{tab:refusal_exp9}\n\\begin{tabular}{lcccc}\n\\toprule\nModel & EN harmful & SL harmful & EN benign & SL benign \\\\\n\\midrule\nGemma-IT & 0.94 & 1.00 & 0.08 & 0.26 \\\\\nGaMS3-Instruct & 0.93 & 0.95 & 0.04 & 0.18 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nGemma over-refuses benign Slovene items at 0.26 vs 0.08 in English, consistent with the criterion-shift pattern. GaMS3 shows a smaller but similar asymmetry (0.18 vs 0.04).\n\n\\subsubsection{Engine-equivalence gate}\n\nThe pre-registered gate required NF4-vs-FP8 first-token agreement of at least 0.90 on 20 fixed prompts per model. Both models reached 0.86 and 0.88 respectively, falling short. The deviation to FP8 quantization (driven by vLLM compatibility on the available GPU) therefore introduces a quantization confound. All results from this experiment carry the label ``FP8 quantization; engine-equivalence gate failed.''\n\n\\subsubsection{Verification}\n\n\\textbf{[Correction (iteration~4, MUST-FIX \\#6b):} The sentence ``independently re-trained on a different random split; headline changed by less than 0.05'' does not appear in experiment~9's output files. What those files record is three code paths agreeing and a model-swap $p = 0.085$. The DeBERTa was trained on 12,639 labels (9,884 train / 2,755 val), not 11,767.\\textbf{]}\n\nTrial pairing was confirmed from Heretic's random-seed logs. Three independent code paths agreed on the headline numbers. Model-swap permutation $p = 0.085$. Spend: \\$0.\n\n\\subsection{Artifact 12: Mechanism test (Experiment~10)}\n\nThis experiment tested two mechanistic hypotheses about why Slovene refusal outlasts English abliteration. The geometry hypothesis predicted that the Slovene-perpendicular component of the refusal direction is geometrically and functionally separate. The induction hypothesis predicted that this perpendicular component induces refusal preferentially in Slovene. Items were 160 TEST harmful + 100 benign + 100 Dolly harmless. The judge was a TF-IDF surrogate trained on 11,767 archived gemini labels (kappa 0.68 EN, 0.82 SL).\n\n\\subsubsection{Geometry: EN and SL refusal directions are nearly collinear}\n\nAt each model's best layer ($L^* = 20$ for Gemma, $L^* = 28$ for GaMS3), the refusal directions extracted from English and Slovene prompts are nearly collinear:\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Geometry of refusal directions at $L^*$ (iteration~3, experiment~10).}\n\\label{tab:geometry}\n\\begin{tabular}{lcccc}\n\\toprule\nModel & $\\cos(r_\\text{EN}, r_\\text{SL})$ & $f$ (SL energy in EN dir.) & Ceiling $\\cos$ & Perp share \\\\\n\\midrule\nGemma-IT & 0.991 [0.989, 0.993] & 0.983 [0.978, 0.986] & 0.999 & 0.13 \\\\\nGaMS3-Instruct & 0.986 [0.984, 0.988] & 0.973 [0.970, 0.975] & 0.998 & 0.16 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe Slovene refusal direction lies almost entirely within the English refusal direction. Only 13--16\\% of the Slovene refusal signal is perpendicular to English. The Gemma-minus-GaMS difference in $f$ at own-$L^*$ is 0.010 [0.005, 0.014], positive but tiny.\n\n\\textbf{[Correction (iteration~4, MUST-FIX \\#9e):} At own-$L^*$, the model difference in $f$ is 0.010, negligible. At the common layer, Gemma-GaMS $f = -0.009$ [$-0.014$, $-0.005$] (GaMS has a larger perpendicular share), band cosines are 0.93/0.89 with perp shares 0.31/0.38, and $d'$ of SL along $r_\\text{EN}$ is 1.37 vs 2.83 (Gemma-GaMS $-1.46$). The sign of the model difference depends on the layer, the same defect that killed alternate~2. M-a is therefore layer-dependent rather than simply refuted.\\textbf{]}\n\n\\textbf{Geometry hypothesis at own-$L^*$: FALSE} for both models at their own best layers. However, at a common layer the model difference reverses ($f = -0.009$ [$-0.014$, $-0.005$], perp share 0.31 vs 0.38, $d'$(SL$|r_\\text{EN}$) 1.37 vs 2.83). The geometry result is layer-dependent.\n\n\\subsubsection{Induction: the Slovene-perpendicular direction does not induce refusal}\n\nAdding the Slovene-perpendicular component ($u_\\text{SLperp}$) to harmless activations at $L^*$ never induced refusal above 50\\% in either model or language. The $\\alpha_{50}$ was right-censored at the maximum tested amplitude (3.0 K-units) for all $u_\\text{SLperp}$ cells. By contrast, the full English refusal direction ($r_\\text{EN}$) reached $\\alpha_{50}$ at 0.91~K for Gemma-EN and 1.32~K for GaMS3-EN. Random directions were also censored. The $u_\\text{SLperp}$ direction is inert as a refusal inducer.\n\n\\textbf{Induction hypothesis verdict: NOT\\_SUPPORTED} for both models.\n\n\\subsubsection{Exploratory: language-identity direction induces Slovene refusal}\n\nThe language-identity direction ($u_\\text{lang}$, extracted from language-classification probes) showed an asymmetric induction pattern. In Gemma, adding $u_\\text{lang}$ at $L^*$ induced Slovene refusal ($\\alpha_{50} = 0.65$ [0.46, 0.79]) but not English refusal (censored at 3.0~K). In GaMS3, the pattern was similar but weaker: Slovene $\\alpha_{50} = 1.78$ [1.32, 2.38], English censored. The model contrast ($\\log R_\\text{lang}$ Gemma minus GaMS3) was 1.03 [0.42, 1.60] under the primary judge. This is exploratory and was not pre-registered.\n\n\\textbf{[Correction (iteration~4, MUST-FIX \\#9b-d):} (b)~$u_\\text{SLperp}$ cut-vs-random is summarised at all three scales: $s{=}0.5$ gives $-0.51$, $s{=}1.0$ gives 0.17 [$-0.09$, 0.44], $s{=}1.5$ gives 0.62 [0.38, 0.97] (excludes 0 but fails EN-invariance gate at $-18$\\,pp EN). (c)~GaMS Lag($E_0$) $= -0.33$ [$-0.70$, 0.07] fails the add-on precondition, so GaMS add-on results are uninformative. (d)~$u_\\text{lang}$ failed the manipulation check in Gemma (manip\\_ok False) and was 77\\% degenerate at $\\alpha_{50}$ in GaMS SL. GaMS EN $\\alpha_{50}$ was 2.96 (not censored as stated).\\textbf{]}\n\n\\subsubsection{Add-on neutralisation: only full $r_\\text{SL}$ ablation closes the lag}\n\n\\textbf{[Correction (iteration~4, MUST-FIX \\#9a):} This is $G_{3,\\text{op}} = \\text{Lag}_\\text{GaMS} - \\text{Lag}_\\text{Gemma}$ at each model's $E_0$ operating point (edited, $\\lambda^*$), not a transfer-curve intercept.\\textbf{]}\n\nAt Gemma's selected abliteration strength ($\\lambda^*$), the baseline lag was $+1.98$ [1.41, 2.73]. Ablating $u_\\text{SLperp}$ at three scales moved the lag to 2.69, 1.34, and 0.45, respectively; the cut-vs-random difference was $-0.51$ at $s{=}0.5$, 0.17 [$-0.09$, 0.44] at $s{=}1.0$, and 0.62 [0.38, 0.97] at $s{=}1.5$ (excludes 0 but fails the EN-invariance gate at $-18$\\,pp EN). Only ablating the full Slovene refusal direction ($A_\\text{SLfull}$) closed the lag ($-6.17$ [$-6.50$, $-5.87$]), at the cost of 50\\% degenerate outputs and 19x KL. GaMS Lag($E_0$) $= -0.33$ [$-0.70$, 0.07] fails the add-on precondition, so the GaMS add-on block is uninformative.\n\n$G_{3,\\text{op}}$ on the experiment~8 SCREEN items (TEST160 harmful subset) was $-2.30$ [$-3.12$, $-1.61$], replicating the sign and approximate magnitude of the experiment~8 lexicon estimate ($-2.36$) under an independent judge on the same item set.\n\n\\subsubsection{Refusal readability: refusal is always readable}\n\n\\textbf{[Correction (iteration~4, MUST-FIX \\#9f):} AUROC $= 1.00$ at layer~8 is flagged ceiling:true. Harmful items are RefusEU and harmless items are Dolly, so this likely reflects dataset-source separability, not ``refusal is always readable''. A same-source harmless control was not run.\\textbf{]}\n\nAcross all abliteration states, AUROC for a fixed linear probe (harmful RefusEU vs harmless Dolly) trained on original-model activations was 1.00 at every layer tested in both models. This is harmful-vs-harmless source separability at ceiling, likely reflecting dataset-source contrast rather than the refusal signal per se. The fixed-probe $d'$ collapses (from 1.37 to 0.25 at the best layer in Gemma under the strongest edit), confirming that abliteration reduces the magnitude of the signal without destroying its separability.\n\n\\subsubsection{Final verdict}\n\n\\textbf{Both the geometry hypothesis and the induction hypothesis are REFUTED.} The Slovene refusal that survives English abliteration is not carried by a separate Slovene direction and cannot be induced by the Slovene-perpendicular component. The lag is a property of the shared refusal subspace, not a geometrically distinct Slovene reserve.\n\n\\subsection{Artifact 13: FINAL confirmation on reserved split (Experiment~11)}\n\n\\textbf{[Correction (iteration~4, MUST-FIX \\#4):} (a)~The quantization was NF4 (8.4\\,GB VRAM), not FP8. Spend: \\$0.\n\n\\subsection{Artifact 14: Utility control (Experiment~12)}\n\nThis experiment measured whether the English-only abliteration edit damages Slovene downstream skills more than English ones, using lm-eval (version~0.4.13) on six zero-shot multiple-choice tasks: ARC-Challenge, BoolQ, HellaSwag, OpenBookQA, PIQA, and Winogrande, with 300 paired English/Slovene items per task. On edited models and on benign content-matched twins, the model difference is not in $c$.\\textbf{]}\n\n\\textbf{[Correction (iteration~4, MUST-FIX \\#13):} Each positive claim is compared with its nearest published neighbour.\\textbf{]}\n\nThree iterations screened the main claim and four alternates against SCORE data (iteration~1), the reserved FINAL evaluation split (iteration~2), and fresh data with mechanism tests and utility controls (iteration~3). The overall GaMS3 Slovene deficit (DiD) is judge-dependent; the meta-analytic estimate is $-0.50$ [$-0.82$, $-0.21$]. On original models and the HARD set, the signal-detection decomposition is robust: the DiD in $d'$ is near zero ($-0.003$), while the DiD in criterion $c$ is $+0.52$ [0.39, 0.67], driven by Gemma over-refusing benign Slovene prompts. This criterion shift replicates across experiments on original models. The criterion-shift finding is therefore specific to the original-model HARD setting. Each artifact's pre-registered verdict: experiment~9 verdict = ESTIMATE; evaluation~2 verdict = ``C-LAG screen holds under validated judges: False'' and ``INCONCLUSIVE/weak-LAG''; experiment~11 verdict = ESTIMATE (``NOT reproduced on reserved data''). Wang et al.~[2] showed full-dose English-direction transfer across 14 languages.\n\nThe utility control (experiment~12) established that the English-only abliteration edit does not damage Slovene downstream skills more than English ones. All macro headroom-normalised losses are below 0.05. The identity calibration arm continues to replicate (FINAL identity DiD $= 3.46$ [2.55, 4.62]).\n\n%% ================================================================\n\\section{Iteration 4}\n%% ================================================================\n\n\\subsection{Strategy}\n\nThree problems guided this iteration, following the reviewer's directive that the budget must go to the readout and a new confirmation rather than more probes.\n\nFirst, the C-LAG sign was consistent but no artifact's pre-registered verdict reached CONFIRM. The main blocker was the edited-row readout: every judge had kappa at most 0.43, and the GaMS-SL false-COMPLY tipping path reached measured error CIs. Iteration~4 addressed this with a paid-judge readout completion (evaluation~3) that applied gemini-2.5-flash and gpt-4.1-mini to all saved edited responses, added translate-then-judge and Rogan-Gladen correction~[25], and pooled across item bodies.\n\nSecond, the mechanism question shifted. The iteration-2 hypothesis update replaced the comprehension-competence framing with two testable accounts: M-OUT (production-side, predicting the lag follows the output language) and M-IN (input-side caution, predicting the lag follows the input language). Experiment~14 tested these with a 2$\\times$3$\\times$3 design crossing input language (EN, SL, HU) with forced output language (EN, SL, HU) at three abliteration doses.\n\nThird, the lag estimate's uncertainty was partly driven by sparse lambda coverage near EN 50\\%. Experiment~15 addressed this with a fine-grained lambda ladder (13 steps for Gemma, 15 for GaMS) on a fresh 300-item RefusEU-TRAIN body disjoint from all prior probes.\n\nFive artifact slots were planned. Slot~2 failed; the other four completed:\n\\begin{enumerate}\n  \\item Evaluation~3 (readout completion): paid-judge re-scoring.\n  \\item Experiment~13 (held-out confirmation, \\textbf{FAILED}): the container lost its GPU about 25 minutes in; no generation or primary label was produced.\n  \\item Experiment~14 (mechanism 2$\\times$3$\\times$3): input language $\\times$ output language $\\times$ dose.\n  \\item Experiment~15 (fine-grained lambda ladder): 13/15-step lambda curve on fresh 300-item body with random-direction controls.\n  \\item Research artifact: prior-art search and fact verification.\n\\end{enumerate}\n\nBecause slot~2 failed, iteration~4 has \\textbf{no held-out confirmation and no RQ2 result}.\n\n\\subsection{Artifact 15: Readout completion with paid judge (Evaluation~3)}\n\nThis evaluation applied the pre-registered paid readout to all saved edited and original rows from experiments~8, 9, 11 and the experiment~10 add-on block. The primary judge was gemini-2.5-flash. The second judge was gpt-4.1-mini on a stratified subset. Translate-then-judge (TTJ) applied NLLB SL-to-EN translation before judging. Blind adjudication used two Claude-family adjudicators (40-row overlap, inter-adjudicator kappa 0.69).\n\n\\subsubsection{Readout gate: FAILS}\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Readout gate (gemini-2.5-flash vs adjudication; iteration~4, evaluation~3).}\n\\label{tab:readout_gate}\n\\begin{tabular}{lcccc}\n\\toprule\nCell & Se [95\\% CI] & Sp [95\\% CI] & kappa gemini-gpt & Pass \\\\\n\\midrule\nGaMS-SL-edited & 0.91 [0.74, 0.97] & 0.73 [0.61, 0.83] & 0.39 & False \\\\\nGemma-SL-edited & 0.99 [0.87, 1.00] & 0.66 [0.43, 0.83] & 0.72 & False \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe paid judge has high sensitivity but specificity of 0.66--0.73 on edited Slovene rows (it over-calls REFUSE), below the pre-registered 0.80 floor. All numbers below are estimates with their CIs, not primary verdicts.\n\n\\subsubsection{Pooled cross-model lag: sign confirmed, edit-induced component is zero}\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Pooled lag estimates (REML + HKSJ, $k = 3$ item bodies, R coding; iteration~4, evaluation~3).}\n\\label{tab:pooled_lag}\n\\begin{tabular}{lcccc}\n\\toprule\nReadout & $G_3$ [95\\% CI] & $G_{3,\\text{edit}}$ [95\\% CI] & IG [95\\% CI] & $I^2$ \\\\\n\\midrule\nRaw primary (gemini) & $-1.17$ [$-1.84$, $-0.50$] & 0.39 [$-1.95$, 2.74] & $-1.15$ [$-1.31$, $-0.99$] & 0.22 \\\\\nRG (unstable) & $-1.79$ [$-7.17$, 3.58] & n/a & $-2.02$ [$-5.40$, 1.35] & 0.00 \\\\\nPPI & $-1.77$ [$-1.89$, $-1.65$] & 0.20 [$-0.72$, 1.11] & $-2.00$ [$-3.19$, $-0.82$] & 0.00 \\\\\nTTJ & $-1.10$ [$-4.67$, 2.47] & 0.33 [$-6.52$, 7.18] & $-1.40$ [$-2.46$, $-0.33$] & 0.59 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe pooled lag is negative under every readout. The edit-induced component is centred near zero in every readout. Nearest neighbours: Deng et al.\\ 2023 (instruction language), Upadhyaya and Sikdar 2026 (output language as outcome, not controlled factor).\n\nHeretic facts: Heretic @3521f86 is a 2.0.0.dev0 snapshot (2026-09-05). Croatian/Serbian/Bosnian make up 22.3\\% of base continued pretraining, a South-Slavic confound.\n\n\\subsection{Not executed or abandoned in iteration~4}\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Iteration-4 components not executed.}\n\\label{tab:not_executed_iter4}\n\\footnotesize\n\\begin{tabular}{llp{4cm}}\n\\toprule\nComponent & Status & Reason \\\\\n\\midrule\nexp13 Heretic edit \\& lambda grid & Not executed & GPU lost \\\\\nexp13 held-out confirmation (B-300) & Not executed & GPU lost \\\\\nexp13 random-dir.\\ controls & Not executed & GPU lost \\\\\nRQ2 natural RefusEU FINAL under edit & Not executed (owed since iter~1) & GPU lost \\\\\nexp13 substitute re-readout (19,195 rows) & Frozen, unlabelled & OpenRouter key limit \\\\\nexp13 judge tier gate & Ran; both tiers FAIL & Sp 0.27--0.55 \\\\\nexp14 harmful-content (ASR) readout & One cell only & Not completed \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n%% ================================================================\n\\section{Iteration 5}\n%% ================================================================\n\n\\subsection{Strategy}\n\nThree goals: (i)~confirm the C-OUT finding on a fresh 294-item body with a new Heretic edit, a suffix-free design, a full 2$\\times$3$\\times$3+controls matrix, and PPI correction (experiment~16); (ii)~run the deferred RefusEU FINAL evaluation with the full 1,300-item pool, random-edit and 256-token controls, and multiple readouts (experiment~17); (iii)~test the R-INCAP question---whether Gemma's Slovene reserve is real safety or production failure---with a StrongREJECT harmful-content endpoint alongside refusal (evaluation~4). Two support artifacts complete the iteration: a paper-number audit (evaluation~5) and a novelty and fact-check update (research~2).\n\n[Correction: C-LAG is now closed in favour of C-OUT. The overall cross-lingual abliteration lag is better characterised as an output-language effect (C-OUT) than as a generic cross-lingual lag (C-LAG).]\n\n[Correction: The novelty verdict for the main claim is downgraded from NOVEL to PARTIALLY OCCUPIED after Addagada~[34] and Nguyen~[35].]\n\n\\subsection{Artifact 19: C-OUT confirmation (Experiment~16)}\n\nThis experiment tested whether the output-language effect (C-OUT)---edited Gemma refusing more when told to write in Slovene than in English---replicates on a fresh 294-item body (146 StrongREJECT, 109 HarmBench, 39 JBB) with a new Heretic edit, using prediction-powered inference (PPI) as the primary estimator.\n\n\\subsubsection{Headline: C-OUT replicates}\n\nThe primary PPI estimate is OUT$_\\text{Gemma} = +2.43$ [$+0.89$, $+5.38$] log-odds: edited Gemma refuses 2.43 log-odds more when told to answer in Slovene than in English. The cross-model contrast dOUT $= -2.31$ [$-5.34$, $-0.68$] excludes zero. GaMS3 shows no output-language effect: OUT$_\\text{GaMS3} = +0.12$ [$-0.47$, $+0.72$], spanning zero. \documentclass[11pt,letterpaper]{article}
\usepackage{graphicx, geometry, amsmath, hyperref, url, booktabs, xcolor, array}
\geometry{margin=1in}
\hypersetup{colorlinks=true, linkcolor=black, citecolor=black, urlcolor=black}

\title{Executive Summary:\\
  Bilingual Refusal Suppression in GaMS3-12B-Instruct vs Gemma-3-12B-IT}
\author{Internal Research Report}
\date{September 2026}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\section{Goal}

This run investigated whether Slovene-taught refusal in GaMS3-12B-Instruct transfers to English and whether an English-only de-censoring tool (Heretic) can strip bilingual refusal as readily as monolingual refusal.  GaMS3 and Gemma-3-12B-IT share a pretrained ancestor (gemma-3-12b-pt) but diverge in their post-training: GaMS3 received Slovene continued pretraining on 140 billion tokens and supervised fine-tuning with approximately 7,000 safety-refusal examples drawn largely from machine-translated Qwen-family responses, while Gemma-IT received Google's standard multilingual post-training.  The run tested a main claim (behaviour-level reach: refusal transfers to English at every hazard-category grain), four pre-registered alternates, and two mechanistic hypotheses, across five iterations totalling 23 artifacts.

\section{What Was Tried}

\textbf{Iteration~1} (5~artifacts): screened the main claim and four alternates on SCORE items.  Measured refusal difference-in-differences, dose contrast, base-checkpoint geometry, persona gating, and Heretic abliteration transfer curves.

\textbf{Iteration~2} (5~artifacts): ran the pre-registered FINAL evaluation on the reserved RefusEU split, tested teacher-inheritance from the Qwen family, re-tested the Heretic transfer curve on a fresh 200-item probe, and reconciled all iteration-1 findings onto a single readout.

\textbf{Iteration~3} (5~artifacts): repaired the experiment~8 readout with validated judges, confirmed the cross-lingual abliteration lag on a fresh 300-item probe with a DeBERTa judge, tested the geometry and induction mechanistic hypotheses, ran the reserved-split FINAL with Hungarian, and ran a utility control on six downstream tasks.

\textbf{Iteration~4} (4~artifacts + 1~failed): completed the readout with paid frontier judges, tested the input-language vs output-language mechanism in a 2$\times$3$\times$3 design, ran a fine-grained 13/15-step lambda ladder on a fresh 300-item body, and conducted a prior-art search.  The held-out confirmation (experiment~13) failed when the container lost its GPU.

\textbf{Iteration~5} (5~artifacts): confirmed the output-language effect (C-OUT) on a fresh 294-item body with PPI correction, ran RefusEU FINAL on 1,300 prompts per language with attack-success measurement, tested whether Gemma's Slovene reserve is real safety or production failure, and audited all paper numbers.

\section{Key Results}

\begin{table}[!htbp]
\centering
\footnotesize
\begin{tabular}{p{4.2cm}lp{4.8cm}}
\toprule
Finding & Source & Number \\
\midrule
R-BASE: lag is pre-edit & Exp.~15 (iter.~4) & $G_{3,\text{edit}} = +0.47$ [$-0.96$, 2.14]; slopes near 1 \\
C-OUT: output language drives residual refusal & Exp.~16 (iter.~5) & OUT$_\text{Gemma}$(PPI) $= +2.43$ [$+0.89$, $+5.38$] \\
Criterion shift (original models, HARD) & Exp.~5 (iter.~2) & $c$ DiD $= +0.52$ [0.39, 0.67]; $d'$ DiD near 0 \\
Identity anchoring & Exp.~5 (iter.~2) & FINAL identity DiD $= 3.46$ [2.55, 4.62] \\
Edit effective on RefusEU FINAL & Exp.~17 (iter.~5) & All 4 paired-edit cells ROBUST \\
Utility: no SL damage & Exp.~12 (iter.~3) & All $H < 0.05$; SL spared vs random \\
R-INCAP: reserve is safety & Eval.~4 (iter.~5) & Harmful content separates at both doses \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\section{What Failed}

\begin{table}[!htbp]
\centering
\footnotesize
\begin{tabular}{p{4cm}p{8.5cm}}
\toprule
Dead end & Reason \\
\midrule
Alternate~2 (base geometry) & delta-$d'$ sign depends on layer; geometry share 4.2\% \\
Alternate~3 (persona gate) & Manipulation check fails; premise (SL surplus) contradicted \\
Alternate~4 (prefill depth) & No readout can validly score prefill continuations \\
Ancestor-direction induction (C4) & Pretrained direction never reached refusal rate 0.50 \\
Geometry hypothesis & EN/SL directions nearly collinear at own-$L^*$ ($\cos \geq 0.986$); layer-dependent at common layer \\
Induction hypothesis & Slovene-perpendicular direction inert as refusal inducer \\
Experiment~13 (held-out confirm.) & GPU lost after 25 minutes; no output produced \\
Dose contrast (main vs alt.~1) & Underpowered across all 5 iterations; MDE exceeds $2m$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\section{Best Result}

The study's most replicable quantitative finding is the signal-detection criterion shift: on original models and HARD items, Gemma-IT shifts its refusal criterion toward refusal on benign Slovene prompts while GaMS3 remains language-invariant.  The DiD in criterion $c$ is $+0.52$ [0.39, 0.67] with the DiD in $d'$ near zero ($-0.003$ [$-0.31$, 0.27]).  This replicates across experiments~5, 9, 14, and~16, and is consistent with a calibration-not-representation account.  The output-language mechanism (C-OUT) explains the residual refusal after abliteration: Gemma refuses 2.43 log-odds more when told to answer in Slovene than in English, with the difference sitting in the criterion, not in discrimination.  These findings indicate that evaluation of multilingual safety should measure criterion and discrimination separately, and that defence against English-only de-censoring should account for the output-language channel.

\section{Open Questions}

\begin{itemize}
  \item The readout gate has never passed; all adjudication is author-LLM, not human.
  \item The frozen-core Heretic procedure (bf16, 80 trials) has never been run.
  \item No artifact has scored natural RefusEU reserved-split prompts under the edit.
  \item The dose contrast (main claim vs alternate~1) remains underpowered.
  \item R-BASE baseline is a ceiling artefact in most item bodies (fragility index 1 in experiment~15).
  \item If R-BASE is correct, the lag is an artefact of model selection, not a property of the abliteration procedure.
  \item The M-OUT finding deserves pre-registered confirmation with human adjudication.
\end{itemize}

\end{document}
```

# Bilingual Refusal Suppression Report

Internal research report documenting five iterations of experiments on bilingual refusal in GaMS3-12B-Instruct vs Gemma-3-12B-IT.

## Layout

| Path | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `report.tex` | LaTeX source for the full 47-page chronological research report |
| `report.pdf` | Compiled report (stays on the run's storage volume) |
| `exec_summary.tex` | LaTeX source for the 3-page executive summary |
| `exec_summary.pdf` | Compiled executive summary (stays on the run's storage volume) |
| `figures/` | Seven pre-rendered vector PDF figures included in the report |
| `.aii/manifest.yaml` | Storage manifest for heavy files |
| `.terminal_claude_agent_struct_out.json` | Structured output metadata |

## Figures

Seven figures are included from the experiment artifacts:

- `fig_forest_did_v0.pdf` — Category-level difference-in-differences forest plot
- `fig_transfer_curve_v0.pdf` — Slovene-vs-English refusal transfer curve
- `fig_hard_sdt_v0.pdf` — Signal-detection decomposition on HARD items
- `fig_transfer_retest_v0.pdf` — Transfer curve re-test on fresh probe
- `fig_lambda_exp9_v0.pdf` — Lambda curve on fresh 300-item probe
- `fig_lambda_ladder_v0.pdf` — Fine-grained lambda ladder
- `fig_cout_forest_v0.pdf` — C-OUT confirmation forest plot

Two figures referenced in the report text were not available as files (`fig_mechanism_2x3`, `fig_rincap_composition`) and are not included.

## Building

```bash

pdflatex -interaction=nonstopmode report.tex

pdflatex -interaction=nonstopmode exec_summary.tex
```

No bibliography file is used; references are typeset inline.

No files are marked for deletion in the manifest. All content is kept.

Prior work on refusal directions~[1] established that a single subspace mediates refusal in English, and Wang et al.~[2] showed that English-extracted refusal directions transfer across 14 languages, but both studies used models whose post-training mixed many languages. Less is known about transfer when safety supervision is concentrated in one language.
