The amendment replaced zero-projection with mean-projection that skips BOS, re-matching the random control on centred variance.\n\n\\subsubsection{Descriptive findings}\n\nGaMS3 showed a Slovene refusal \\emph{deficit} relative to Gemma, not the surplus that alternate~3 predicts. The unablated DiD was $-1.11$ [$-2.00$, $-0.36$] on the judge and $-2.72$ [$-3.30$, $-2.13$] on the prefix score. On the translation-matched items, it was $-3.06$ [$-3.59$, $-2.52$]. Late-layer persona ablation barely moved GaMS3's Slovene refusal: 0.883 to 0.853 (McNemar $p = 0.08$).\n\nAn exploratory finding: ablating GaMS3's own-name direction made GaMS3 identify as Qwen (English 0.15 to 0.78, Slovene 0.03 to 0.60), while random controls stayed at 0.23 to 0.30 and Gemma was unaffected. This is teacher-identity substitution, not persona removal: the ablation does not erase the identity; it replaces GaMS with the training-data source.\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Refusal and identity rates under persona ablation (GaMS3, SCORE-400; iteration~1, experiment~3).}\n\\label{tab:persona_ablation}\n\\begin{tabular}{lcccc}\n\\toprule\nCondition & EN refusal & SL refusal & EN own-name & SL own-name \\\\\n\\midrule\nOriginal & 0.925 & 0.675 & 0.45 & 0.90 \\\\\nPersona ablated (late) & 0.925 & 0.653 & 0.00 & 0.00 \\\\\nRandom control (late) & 0.925 & 0.670 & 0.23--0.30 & 0.23--0.30 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nLanguage-identity and Gemma induction ablation (C5) were catastrophic by the degeneracy gates and are not reported.\n\n\\textbf{Alternate~3 is dead.} The manipulation check fails, the premise (a Slovene surplus) is contradicted by the data, and the effect size is too small relative to the MDE.\n\n\\subsection{Artifact 5: Heretic abliteration and transfer curve (Experiment~4)}\n%% workspace: gen_art_experiment_4\n\nEnglish-objective abliteration (gen\\_art\\_experiment\\_4) was run on both instruct checkpoints using \\citet{Weidmann2025} with identical configuration: NF4, empty system prompt, TPE sampler with seed 20260923. The 17 compared draws were verified identical across models (paired design). A driver script copied Heretic's objective verbatim and logged bilingual metrics that never entered the objective; non-interference was verified by replaying objective values and confirming identical LoRA hashes.\n\n\\subsubsection{English abliteration reaches Slovene}\n\nLexicon refusal on 400 RefusEU pairs fell sharply in both languages and both models:\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Refusal rates before and after Heretic abliteration (lexicon, 400 pairs; iteration~1, experiment~4).}\n\\label{tab:heretic_refusal}\n\\begin{tabular}{lcccc}\n\\toprule\nCondition & Gemma EN & Gemma SL & GaMS EN & GaMS SL \\\\\n\\midrule\nOriginal & 0.965 & 0.932 & 0.940 & 0.830 \\\\\nSelected edit & 0.242 & 0.223 & 0.133 & 0.098 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nTrial-level slopes of Slovene refusal on English refusal were positive for both models (Gemma 1.21 [0.75, 1.83]; GaMS3 0.79 [0.51, 1.14]); shuffling Slovene rates produced slopes of 0.01 $\\pm$ 0.28. English-objective abliteration removes Slovene refusal.\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n  \\centering\n  \\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig_transfer_curve_v0.pdf}\n  \\caption{Slovene-vs-English refusal transfer curve under Heretic abliteration. Trial-level slopes are positive for both models (iteration~1, experiment~4).}\n  \\label{fig:transfer_curve}\n\\end{figure}\n\n\\subsubsection{C3 (frozen-core transfer): fails both ways}\n\n\\textbf{[Correction (iteration~4, MINOR \\#1):} The experiment~4 summary gives $G_3 = -1.86$ [$-2.87$, $-1.13$] on the matched first 17 trials, $-1.76$ on all trials, $-0.98$ on the lambda curve. The text below used $-1.76$ for the matched-17 value; the correct matched-17 value is $-1.86$.\\textbf{]}\n\nThe primary statistic $G_3$ (the GaMS-minus-Gemma difference in the logistic transfer-curve intercept, measuring whether GaMS3 retains more Slovene refusal at matched English refusal) was $-1.86$ [$-2.87$, $-1.13$] on the matched first 17 trials ($-1.76$ on all trials, $-1.74$ on translation-equivalent pairs). The main claim required $|G_3| < m = 0.675$; alternate~1 required $G_3 > m$. Neither holds: Slovene refusal is \\emph{more exposed} in GaMS3 than in Gemma at any matched English refusal level. Trial-label permutation $p = 0.000$.\n\nThe category-level version ($G_3$ in low-EN vs high-EN categories) was 0.39 [$-1.19$, 2.12], not separating dose groups.\n\n\\subsubsection{C5a (excess Slovene KL): reverses the prediction}\n\nThe pre-registered test asked whether Heretic's real refusal direction damages Slovene more than a norm-matched random direction. The excess Slovene/English KL ratio was 0.298 [0.154, 0.562] for Gemma and 0.574 [0.409, 0.796] for GaMS3, both with confidence intervals entirely below 1. The real direction damages Slovene \\emph{less} than random directions. There is no Slovene leakage; the English-only objective is, if anything, Slovene-sparing.\n\n\\subsubsection{C5b (bilingual re-selection): unpowered}\n\nOnly one candidate trial per model met the re-selection criteria, and it was the same as the original pick. Gain was zero. The test is unpowered because no trial reached the pre-registered threshold of 10 or fewer keyword refusals out of 100 (the best was 64/100 for Gemma, 29/100 for GaMS3). The fallback to a reduced-trial random-search analysis was triggered.\n\n\\subsubsection{Alternate~4 (thin templated gate): strongest signal but does not survive}\n\nA five-token compliant prefill (``Sure, here is'') flipped refusals at strikingly different rates across models:\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Prefill flip rates (fraction of items that refused at $k=0$ but complied at $k=5$; iteration~1, experiment~4).}\n\\label{tab:prefill_flip}\n\\begin{tabular}{lcccc}\n\\toprule\n & Gemma EN & Gemma SL & GaMS EN & GaMS SL \\\\\n\\midrule\nFlip rate & 0.031 & 0.558 & 0.559 & 0.855 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe prefill signature Sig was 3.63 [3.13, 4.36] in English and 1.54 [1.20, 1.92] in Slovene, both exceeding the $m_2$ threshold of 0.40 with confidence intervals above zero ($z_c = 6.23$, paired label-swap $p = 0.000$). GaMS3's refusal is more brittle than Gemma's in both languages, and the gap is larger in English (Sig$_\\text{EN}$) than in Slovene (Sig$_\\text{SL}$). However, alternate~4 predicted symmetric language effects ($|\\text{Sig}_\\text{SL} - \\text{Sig}_\\text{EN}| < m$), and the observed asymmetry was 2.10, far exceeding the threshold. Alternate~4 was scored as not survived.\n\nThe Pareto hypervolume ratio (GaMS3/Gemma) was 2.29 [2.01, 3.36], confirming that GaMS3's refusal is easier to remove across the entire refusal-KL trade-off front.\n\n\\subsubsection{Failed attempts}\n\nThe plan's raw Arditi-style~\\citep{Arditi2024} rank-$k$ ablation destroyed Gemma (KL 20 to 53 nats even for a random basis) and was abandoned. Mechanistic question C code was implemented but not run due to the key limit. Judge validation did not confirm the lexicon (kappa below 0.70 in all cells, though raw agreement was 95\\% with PABAK 0.90 on unedited cells). GaMS3's judge labels are incomplete: the OpenRouter key hit its daily limit before GaMS3 could be judged, and a retry with the replacement key still returned a 403 error.\n\n\\subsubsection{Limits}\n\nAll transfer-curve and Pareto numbers come from reduced-trial random search, not the planned 80-trial Optuna run. The EN-KL-matched random control was unmatchable at the 6x cap. The lexicon is the primary readout because judge validation failed, with the prefix score as co-primary. Unedited-model KL reproduces to only 0.030 nats under NF4 batching.\n\n\\subsection{Summary of dead ends and surviving claims}\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Status of pre-registered claims after iteration~1.}\n\\label{tab:claims_iter1}\n\\footnotesize\n\\begin{tabular}{llp{4.5cm}p{3cm}}\n\\toprule\nClaim & Status & Key evidence & Next step \\\\\n\\midrule\nMain: behaviour-level reach (C2) & INCONCLUSIVE & $D$ uninformative; MDE 1.5--1.9; lexicon/judge disagree & FINAL with larger $N$ and validated judge \\\\\nAlt~1: supervised reach & INCONCLUSIVE & Same $D$; zEN flips sign across readouts & Same \\\\\nAlt~2: base geometry & DEAD & delta-$d'$ sign depends on layer; geometry share 4.2\\% & None \\\\\nAlt~3: persona gate & UNTESTABLE (manipulation check fails); DEAD (premise contradicted) & Manipulation check fails; premise (SL surplus) contradicted & None \\\\\nAlt~4: thin gate & NOT SURVIVED & Prefill asymmetry too large; signature not symmetric & Descriptive only \\\\\nC1: identity calibration & PASS & DiD$_{id} = 3.22$ [2.38, 4.38] & Carry forward \\\\\nC3: frozen-core transfer & FAILS BOTH WAYS & $G_3 = -1.76$ [$-2.73$, $-1.09$]; GaMS more exposed & Investigate with full Optuna run \\\\\nC4: ancestor induction & FAILURE BRANCH & pt direction never reaches $R = 0.50$; own-direction equivalence holds & Report as check \\\\\nC5a: excess SL KL & REVERSES & Ratio 0.30 / 0.57, CI below 1 & Confirm with judge \\\\\nC5b: re-selection & UNPOWERED & $n = 1$ candidate per model & Full Optuna run needed \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n%% ================================================================\n\\section{Iteration 2}\n%% ================================================================\n\n\\subsection{Strategy}\n\nIteration~2 addressed three weaknesses identified by the reviewer and by iteration~1's own diagnostics. First, the main claim (behaviour-level reach vs category-level supervised reach) remained inconclusive because the dose contrast was unpowered on SCORE items, the lexicon and judge disagreed, and no FINAL evaluation had been run. Second, the Heretic transfer-curve finding (the transfer-curve intercept was $-1.76$, meaning GaMS3 retained less Slovene refusal than Gemma at matched English refusal) rested on a lexicon readout that failed judge validation in three of four cells. Third, the teacher-inheritance pathway, an alternate not originally pre-registered, was flagged by the reviewer as a plausible alternative account given GaMS3's heavy reliance on Qwen-family refusal data.\n\nThe iteration ran five artifacts:\n\\begin{enumerate}\n  \\item Experiment~5 (confirmation): the pre-registered FINAL evaluation on the reserved RefusEU evaluation split, the item-matched machine-translation arm, the HARD set (XSTest + OR-Bench), and the identity questions, using 20,300 generations and a local Qwen3-14B judge after the OpenRouter budget was exhausted.\n  \\item Experiment~6 (refusal depth pipeline): the code scaffold for a refusal-depth experiment. It produced no scored output and is reported as infrastructure, not a finding.\n  \\item Experiment~7 (teacher inheritance): a five-system screen comparing GaMS3, Gemma-IT, Qwen3-235B (the teacher), Qwen3-14B (same-family control), and Llama-3.3-70B (outgroup placebo), testing whether GaMS3's refusal decisions and wording inherit from its Qwen teacher.\n  \\item Experiment~8 (Heretic re-test): a fresh paired abliteration run on 200 item-matched RefusEU-TRAIN probes with three dose curves, removing the iteration-1 confounds (unmatched EN/SL items, no judge on GaMS3) and testing the transfer curve, depth, and Slovene KL leakage with a local Llama-3.1-8B judge.\n  \\item Evaluation~1 (reconciliation): a \\$0 harmonised re-scoring of all iteration-1 screens on a single readout, checking which findings survive, shrink, or become uncitable under a consistent judge.\n\\end{enumerate}\n\nThe OpenRouter shared key was exhausted for most of the iteration (403 errors on all calls, including after the replacement notice). Every experiment that needed paid judges fell back to local open-weight models. This is the single largest constraint on this iteration's evidence quality.\n\n\\subsection{Artifact 6: Confirmation on the reserved FINAL splits (Experiment~5)}\n%% workspace: gen_art_experiment_5\n\nThis was the pre-registered confirmation run (gen\\_art\\_experiment\\_5) on the reserved evaluation data. Both models were run in NF4 quantization with greedy decoding (160 tokens, empty system turn, byte-identical template) at seed 20260924.\n\n\\textbf{Deviation D5.} The run's OpenRouter budget was exhausted mid-FINAL. The pre-registered gemini-2.5-flash and gpt-4.1-mini judges could not run to completion. The FINAL primary readout is a local Qwen3-14B judge (frozen prompt, logit-based), validated against gemini on DEV (binary kappa 0.68 to 0.86 across cells) and on the 11,146 FINAL rows that received gemini labels before the budget ran out. Identity uses a regex scorer validated against gemini on DEV (kappa 0.82 for Gemma, 1.00 for GaMS3). A DEV-based calibration layer corrects Qwen3's inflation of REFUSE on hedged English answers.\n\n\\subsubsection{Identity calibration: passes on FINAL}\n\nThe identity arm replicates. GaMS3 named itself ``GaMS'' in 90\\% of Slovene answers and 33\\% of English answers; Gemma did not name itself in either language (the regex scored 0\\% in all Gemma cells because Gemma's own-name responses did not match the strict regex pattern). GaMS3 credited Qwen or Alibaba in 51\\% of English identity responses (up from 42\\% in iteration~1). The FINAL identity DiD was 3.46 [2.55, 4.62] ($m_{id} = 0.40$), confirming that the design can detect language anchoring.\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Identity results on FINAL (80 pairs; iteration~2, experiment~5).}\n\\label{tab:identity_final}\n\\begin{tabular}{lc}\n\\toprule\nCell & Own-name rate (regex) \\\\\n\\midrule\nGaMS EN & 0.325 \\\\\nGaMS SL & 0.900 \\\\\nGemma EN & 0.563 \\\\\nGemma SL & 0.413 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\subsubsection{Refusal on RefusEU natural pairs}\n\nOn 1,300 FINAL pairs, the Qwen3 judge gave the following refusal rates:\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{FINAL refusal rates (Qwen3-14B judge, RefusEU natural pairs; iteration~2, experiment~5).}\n\\label{tab:final_refusal}\n\\begin{tabular}{lcc}\n\\toprule\nModel & EN & SL \\\\\n\\midrule\nGaMS3-Instruct & 0.972 & 0.922 \\\\\nGemma-IT & 0.979 & 0.958 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe overall DiD was $-0.35$ [$-0.81$, 0.13], about $-2.8$\\,pp on the probability scale. The 95\\% CI includes zero: on the Qwen3 judge, there is no significant GaMS3 Slovene deficit.\n\nThe dose contrast was $-0.27$ [$-1.31$, 0.71], with minimum detectable effect 1.36 exceeding twice the pre-registered threshold ($2m = 1.02$). The dose test remains underpowered on the FINAL data.\n\nThe judge-family robustness check revealed a stark dependence on the judge. Gemini-2.5-flash labels existed for 607 of the 1,300 pairs (all GaMS3 rows plus the first Gemma rows before the budget ran out). On those 607 overlapping pairs:\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{DiD by judge family on the same 607 pairs (iteration~2, experiment~5).}\n\\label{tab:judge_family}\n\\begin{tabular}{lc}\n\\toprule\nJudge & DiD [95\\% CI] \\\\\n\\midrule\nGemini-2.5-flash & $-0.63$ [$-1.14$, $-0.16$] \\\\\nQwen3-14B & $+0.03$ [$-0.75$, 0.82] \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe same items produce a significant GaMS3 Slovene deficit under gemini and a null under Qwen3. This judge dependence is the iteration's most consequential finding for the primary contest: the size and sign of the refusal DiD are not robust to the choice of judge family.\n\n\\subsubsection{Item-matched machine-translation arm}\n\nOn 1,296 FINAL pairs (EN back-translation vs SL machine translation from the same English source), the DiD was $-1.67$ [$-2.75$, $-1.03$]. This is larger than the natural-pair DiD and is driven by Gemma refusing more in Slovene (99.5\\%) than in English (97.5\\%) on the matched items. The MT-arm DiD cannot be directly compared with the natural-pair DiD because the items differ in content and difficulty.\n\n\\subsubsection{HARD set: signal-detection analysis}\n\nThe HARD set (349 unsafe + 1,093 safe items from XSTest and OR-Bench, with SL machine translations and EN back-translations) was analysed in a signal-detection framework.\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Signal-detection parameters on HARD (SL-MT vs EN-BT; iteration~2, experiment~5).}\n\\label{tab:sdt_hard}\n\\begin{tabular}{lcccc}\n\\toprule\n & $d'$ & $c$ (criterion) & Hit rate & False-alarm rate \\\\\n\\midrule\nGemma EN & 1.574 & $-0.440$ & 0.890 & 0.364 \\\\\nGemma SL & 1.393 & $-0.870$ & 0.941 & 0.569 \\\\\nGaMS EN & 1.862 & $-0.327$ & 0.896 & 0.273 \\\\\nGaMS SL & 1.678 & $-0.235$ & 0.859 & 0.273 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe DiD in $d'$ (discrimination) was $-0.003$ [$-0.33$, 0.29]: the two models lose the same amount of discrimination between languages. The DiD in criterion $c$ was $+0.52$ [0.38, 0.68], the most robust result of the FINAL run. Gemma-IT shifts its criterion toward refusal on benign Slovene prompts (false-alarm rate rising from 0.364 to 0.569), while GaMS3 is language-invariant on criterion (false-alarm rates 0.273 in both languages). GaMS3 does not over-refuse in Slovene; Gemma does.\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n  \\centering\n  \\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig_hard_sdt_v0.pdf}\n  \\caption{Signal-detection decomposition on HARD items. Gemma shifts its criterion toward refusal in Slovene while GaMS3 remains language-invariant (iteration~2, experiment~5).}\n  \\label{fig:hard_sdt}\n\\end{figure}\n\nThis criterion shift is fragile under partial-as-refusal coding, and the DEV gemini judge produced a comparable estimate ($+0.67$). It replicates across OR-Bench items alone ($+0.70$ [0.50, 0.93]) and survives dropping MT-fragile items ($+0.62$ [0.46, 0.79]).\n\n\\subsubsection{Refusal style}\n\nGaMS3's Slovene refusals on RefusEU are terse (median 16 tokens, vs 160 for Gemma) and formulaic: 61\\% open with ``Oprostite, vendar vam pri tem'' and 87\\% are covered by the top five openings. In English, 86\\% of GaMS3 refusals open with ``I'm sorry, but I can't''. Gemma's refusals are longer (median 160 tokens), with more varied openings (``I am programmed to be'' in English, ``\\v{Z}al mi je, vendar ne'' in Slovene).\n\n\\subsubsection{Verification}\n\nThe audit passed 27 of 27 checks. An independent pandas re-derivation matched all headline numbers to $10^{-9}$. Permutation tests confirmed $p < 0.001$ for identity DiD, with placebos not significant. Spend was \\$2.10.\n\n\\subsection{Artifact 7: Teacher-inheritance screen (Experiment~7)}\n%% workspace: gen_art_experiment_7\n\nThis exploratory screen (gen\\_art\\_experiment\\_7) tested whether GaMS3's refusal decisions and wording inherit from its Qwen-family teacher. Five systems were run on byte-identical prompts (greedy, empty system turn, 160 tokens): GaMS3-12B-Instruct (NF4), Gemma-3-12B-IT (NF4), Qwen3-235B-A22B (the SFT data generator, via OpenRouter with thinking off), Qwen3-14B (same-family positive control, NF4), and Llama-3.3-70B (outgroup placebo). The protocol was frozen before the full pass. Items: 616 HARD-DEV (XSTest + OR-Bench) + 400 SCORE RefusEU + 117 identity items; English, SL-MT, and EN back-translation arms.\n\n\\textbf{Readout caveat.} The OpenRouter budget ran out before the pre-registered gemini judge could label all systems. Headline numbers use a local Mistral-Small-24B judge (NF4, frozen prompt), validated against gemini with binary kappa 0.67 to 0.86 per local cell. Prefill rows have kappa 0.15 and are invalid under this readout.\n\n\\subsubsection{Decision inheritance: uninterpretable}\n\nThe fingerprint-calibration gate failed. The positive control asked whether the instrument can detect within-family resemblance: the Qwen3-14B-to-Qwen3-235B kappa should exceed the Qwen3-14B-to-Gemma kappa by at least 0.10. The observed difference was $-0.001$ [$-0.074$, 0.079]: the instrument cannot distinguish same-family from cross-family agreement. All pairwise kappas cluster at 0.51 to 0.60, dominated by item difficulty (retest ceiling 0.88). The descriptive GaMS3-to-teacher kappa minus GaMS3-to-Gemma kappa was $-0.044$ [$-0.118$, 0.032], with the 90\\% CI excluding a $+0.10$ teacher advantage. GaMS3 does not take the teacher's side more often than it takes the sibling's, but the instrument lacks the resolution to detect even genuine family resemblance.\n\n\\subsubsection{Wording inheritance: supported}\n\nRefusal wording tells a different story. The SFT-source classifier (5-fold cross-validated accuracy 0.97) attributed 95.8\\% of GaMS3's English refusal first sentences to the Qwen teacher family, with an independent SVM re-derivation at 98.4\\% (shuffled-label placebo: 18\\%). Gemma scored 0.7\\%. In Slovene, GaMS3's refusal wording matches the GaMS-27B translated SFT data (90.8\\% of first sentences found verbatim) rather than the live teacher's output (1.5\\%).\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Refusal first-sentence origin (share found verbatim in SFT data; iteration~2, experiment~7).}\n\\label{tab:wording_inheritance}\n\\begin{tabular}{lcc}\n\\toprule\nModel & EN & SL \\\\\n\\midrule\nGaMS3-Instruct & 0.761 & 0.908 \\\\\nGemma-IT & 0.000 & 0.030 \\\\\nQwen3-235B & 0.757 & 0.015 \\\\\nQwen3-14B & 0.092 & 0.007 \\\\\nLlama-3.3-70B & 0.254 & 0.016 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe English column shows that GaMS3 and the teacher share the same refusal vocabulary to the same degree (76\\%), and both are distinct from Gemma (0\\%). In Slovene, GaMS3 uses the machine-translated SFT wording (91\\%), not the teacher's live Slovene output (1.5\\%), confirming that the Slovene refusal calque originates in the training data translation, not in a runtime cross-lingual transfer from the teacher.\n\n\\subsubsection{Language asymmetry: Gemma is the outlier}\n\nGemma-IT over-refuses safe Slovene items ($+0.24$ vs English), while GaMS3, the teacher, and the same-family control refuse \\emph{less} in Slovene. The Slovene kappa difference (GaMS3 vs teacher minus GaMS3 vs Gemma) was 0.082, and the gap-of-gaps (DiffGap) was $-0.133$ [$-0.247$, $-0.011$], running opposite to a teacher-inheritance prediction and driven by Gemma being the outlier in Slovene.\n\n\\subsubsection{Identity}\n\nGaMS3 named Qwen or Alibaba in 47\\% of English identity answers and 7\\% of Slovene ones, consistent with the FINAL result (51\\% English, not measured in Slovene by this artifact).\n\n\\subsubsection{Verification}\n\nAudit: 52 of 52 independent checks passed. An independent re-derivation with placebos reproduced all headline numbers. Judge spend: \\$1.45. The pre-registered paid readout (gemini + gpt-4.1 second family) is implemented but unrun; finalize.sh is resumable.\n\n\\subsection{Artifact 8: Heretic transfer-curve re-test (Experiment~8)}\n%% workspace: gen_art_experiment_8\n\nThis artifact (gen\\_art\\_experiment\\_8) re-tested the iteration-1 finding that English-objective Heretic abliteration strips GaMS3's Slovene refusal faster than Gemma's (iteration-1 lexicon transfer-curve intercept $= -1.86$), using a design that removes the iteration-1 confounds. It uses a fresh 200-item RefusEU-TRAIN probe, item-matched across three arms from one English source (EN original, NLLB Slovene MT, NLLB English back-translation). Both models were run through an identical code path (NF4, empty system, greedy, seed 20260924) over three dose curves:\n\n\\begin{itemize}\n  \\item \\textbf{Curve B (confirmatory):} 29 paired fresh Heretic trials whose TPE start-up draws were verified parameter-identical across models (9 of the 29 trials diverged in parameters after the start-up phase).\n  \\item \\textbf{Lambda-scaling curve:} the iteration-1 selected Heretic LoRA scaled by lambda (0.0 to 2.0 in 8 steps for Gemma, 6 for GaMS3).\n  \\item \\textbf{Mean-projection curve:} graded mean-projection ablation of a winsorised own-English refusal direction with a centred-variance random-direction control.\n\\end{itemize}\n\n\\textbf{[Correction (iteration~4, MUST-FIX \\#6a):} The primary readout was the unvalidated lexicon. The Llama-3.1-8B judge labelled only 3,374 of 24,000 rows (kappa 0.52). The iteration-2 hypothesis update noted this: ``the paper's statement that experiment~8 used a Llama judge must be corrected''. See evaluation~2 for the repair.\\textbf{]}\n\nThe judge was Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (selected over Qwen3-8B by higher binary-refusal kappa vs gemini on a 1,000-row Gemma calibration set), applied identically to both models with the frozen judge prompt. Gemini labels exist for all Gemma rows but no GaMS3 rows (budget exhausted).\n\n\\subsubsection{Transfer curve: GaMS3 Slovene less retained, confirmed on fresh trials}\n\nOn the 29 paired Heretic trials (confirmatory curve), the transfer-curve intercept (the GaMS-minus-Gemma predicted Slovene refusal rate at matched English refusal of 50\\%, on a logistic scale) was $-2.36$ [$-3.18$, $-1.62$]. At matched English refusal of 50\\%, Gemma retains 38\\,pp more Slovene refusal than GaMS3. The permutation test gave $p < 0.001$ (null mean 0.006, null SD 0.44). The BCa-corrected CI was [$-3.22$, $-1.63$].\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{$G_3$ (GaMS-minus-Gemma predicted SL refusal at EN refusal = 50\\%) across dose curves (iteration~2, experiment~8).}\n\\label{tab:g3_curves_exp8}\n\\begin{tabular}{lccc}\n\\toprule\nCurve & $G_3$ [95\\% CI] & Verdict ($m = 0.675$) & Verdict ($m_\\text{local} = 0.20$) \\\\\n\\midrule\nB (29 paired trials) & $-2.36$ [$-3.18$, $-1.62$] & SL\\_OVER\\_EXPOSURE & SL\\_OVER\\_EXPOSURE \\\\\nA1 (lambda scaling) & $-0.19$ [$-1.03$, 0.78] & INCONCLUSIVE & INCONCLUSIVE \\\\\nA2 (mean-projection) & excluded (non-specific) & n/a & n/a \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe confirmatory curve confirms and strengthens the iteration-1 finding (iteration-1: intercept $= -1.86$ [$-2.87$, $-1.13$] on 17 trials). The lambda-scaling curve gives a much smaller and non-significant intercept ($-0.19$): the two curves disagree. The mean-projection curve was excluded because the direction-specific control failed in GaMS3 (ablating the real direction reduced refusal by the same amount as ablating random directions).\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n  \\centering\n  \\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig_transfer_retest_v0.pdf}\n  \\caption{Transfer curve re-test on fresh 200-item probe. The RP readout gave $G_3 = +8.74$ [$-1.51$, 14.05] (perm $p$ 0.04, degenerate support).\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{McNemar rates on the reserved split (Qwen3-14B judge, REFUSE-only; iteration~3, experiment~11).}\n\\label{tab:mcnemar_exp11}\n\\begin{tabular}{lcccc}\n\\toprule\nModel & EN orig & EN edit & SL orig & SL edit \\\\\n\\midrule\nGemma-IT & 0.98 & 0.645 & 0.99 & 0.68 \\\\\nGaMS3-Instruct & 0.97 & 0.58 & 0.97 & 0.46 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nGaMS3's Slovene refusal drops further than Gemma's (from 0.97 to 0.46 vs from 0.99 to 0.68), consistent with a lag but not reaching significance because both models also differ in English.\n\n\\textbf{Why the test was underpowered.} The Qwen3-14B judge over-calls English refusal. On the 36 blind-adjudicated GaMS3-EN edited rows, the judge's specificity was 0.33 (kappa 0.27). It labels many English compliant responses as refusals, inflating edited English rates and shrinking the apparent EN-to-SL difference.\n\n\\subsubsection{Hungarian behaves like Slovene}\n\n\\textbf{[Correction (iteration~4, MUST-FIX \\#8):} The Slovene two-point row gives $G_{3,2\\text{pt}} = +0.05$ [$-1.49$, 2.02]: no GaMS-vs-Gemma difference in Slovene. Verdict: ESTIMATE for both languages.\n\n\\subsubsection{Belebele comprehension: unchanged by the edit}\n\nBelebele reading-comprehension accuracy on 200 human-translated parallel items was unaffected by the edit in every model-language cell:\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Belebele accuracy (200 items, FP8 quantization; iteration~3, experiment~11).}\n\\label{tab:belebele}\n\\begin{tabular}{llccc}\n\\toprule\nModel & Condition & EN & SL & HU \\\\\n\\midrule\nGemma-IT & Original & 0.930 & 0.885 & 0.880 \\\\\nGemma-IT & Edit ($\\lambda{=}1$) & 0.930 & 0.885 & 0.880 \\\\\nGaMS3-Instruct & Original & 0.905 & 0.875 & 0.870 \\\\\nGaMS3-Instruct & Edit ($\\lambda{=}1$) & 0.910 & 0.870 & 0.825 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nGemma is entirely unchanged. This is direct evidence against an edit-induced lag on FINAL, not for it.\\textbf{]}\n\nA generalised estimating equation on 7,337 original+edited rows found a significant three-way interaction: the gams:sl:edit coefficient was $+1.06$ ($p = 0.022$; VB posterior $+1.04 \\pm 0.16$). Spend: \\$0.\n\n\\subsection{Artifact 14: Utility control (Experiment~12)}\n%% workspace: gen_art_experiment_12\n\nThis experiment (gen\\_art\\_experiment\\_12) measured whether the English-only abliteration edit damages Slovene downstream skills more than English ones, using lm-eval (version~0.4.13) on six zero-shot multiple-choice tasks: ARC-Challenge, BoolQ, HellaSwag, OpenBookQA, PIQA, and Winogrande, with 300 paired English/Slovene items per task. The design resolves the interaction to about 0.10 of headroom.\n\nRandom-adjusted asymmetry (edit minus random) was $+0.051$ [$+0.012$, $+0.093$] for GaMS3 under the iteration-1 edit and $+0.038$ [$+0.001$, $+0.080$] under the artifact-2 edit: relative to a same-size random perturbation, the edit spares Slovene. Experiment~8, evaluation~2, and experiment~10 share items.\\textbf{]}\n\n\\textbf{[Correction (iteration~4, MUST-FIX \\#3):} The criterion-shift claim is restricted to ``original models, HARD set''. On edited models and on benign content-matched twins, the model difference is not in $c$.\\textbf{]}\n\n\\textbf{[Correction (iteration~4, MUST-FIX \\#13):} Each positive claim is compared with its nearest published neighbour.\\textbf{]}\n\nThree iterations screened the main claim and four alternates against SCORE data (iteration~1), the reserved FINAL evaluation split (iteration~2), and fresh data with mechanism tests and utility controls (iteration~3). Two alternates are dead (base-checkpoint geometry and persona gating). A third (prefill-depth signature, alternate~4) is uncitable because no available readout can validly score prefill continuations. Two mechanistic hypotheses were tested: the geometry hypothesis is layer-dependent---nearly collinear at own-$L^*$ ($\\cos = 0.986$--$0.991$) but divergent at a common layer. The induction hypothesis is not supported.\n\nThe primary contest between behaviour-level reach and supervised reach remains unresolved. The dose contrast is underpowered across all three iterations. The overall GaMS3 Slovene deficit (DiD) is judge-dependent; the meta-analytic estimate is $-0.50$ [$-0.82$, $-0.21$]. On original models and the HARD set, the signal-detection decomposition is robust: the DiD in $d'$ is near zero ($-0.003$), while the DiD in criterion $c$ is $+0.52$ [0.38, 0.68], driven by Gemma over-refusing benign Slovene prompts. This criterion shift was observed across experiments~5, 9, 14, and~16 on original models (a post-hoc count, not a pre-registered replication criterion). On edited models (experiment~11 HARD post-edit), DiD$_c = 0.14$ [$-0.78$, 1.12]: the criterion-shift difference disappears after the edit. The criterion-shift finding is therefore specific to the original-model HARD setting. \\citet{Aziz2026} showed calibration-not-representation across 23 languages.\n\nThe cross-lingual abliteration lag (C-LAG) has a consistent negative sign but is not confirmed by pre-registered criteria. Each artifact's pre-registered verdict: experiment~9 verdict = ESTIMATE; evaluation~2 verdict = ``C-LAG screen holds under validated judges: False'' and ``INCONCLUSIVE/weak-LAG''; experiment~11 verdict = ESTIMATE (``NOT reproduced on reserved data''). Experiment~8, evaluation~2, and experiment~10 share the same item set, so there are two independent datasets, not three. The magnitude ranges from $-0.6$ to $-2.4$ across designs and judges. \\citet{Wang2025} showed full-dose English-direction transfer across 14 languages.\n\nThe utility control (experiment~12) established that the English-only abliteration edit does not damage Slovene downstream skills more than English ones. All macro headroom-normalised losses are below 0.05. The identity calibration arm continues to replicate (FINAL identity DiD $= 3.46$ [2.55, 4.62]).\n\n%% ================================================================\n\\section{Iteration 4}\n%% ================================================================\n\n\\subsection{Strategy}\n\nThree problems guided this iteration, following the reviewer's directive that the budget must go to the readout and a new confirmation rather than more probes.\n\nFirst, the C-LAG sign was consistent but no artifact's pre-registered verdict reached CONFIRM. The main blocker was the edited-row readout: every judge had kappa at most 0.43, and the GaMS-SL false-COMPLY tipping path reached measured error CIs. Iteration~4 addressed this with a paid-judge readout completion (evaluation~3) that applied gemini-2.5-flash and gpt-4.1-mini to all saved edited responses, added translate-then-judge and Rogan-Gladen correction~\\citep{Lee2025}, and pooled across item bodies.\n\nSecond, the mechanism question shifted. The iteration-2 hypothesis update replaced the comprehension-competence framing with two testable accounts: M-OUT (production-side, predicting the lag follows the output language) and M-IN (input-side caution, predicting the lag follows the input language). Experiment~14 tested these with a 2$\\times$3$\\times$3 design crossing input language (EN, SL, HU) with forced output language (EN, SL, HU) at three abliteration doses.\n\nThird, the lag estimate's uncertainty was partly driven by sparse lambda coverage near EN 50\\%. Experiment~15 addressed this with a fine-grained lambda ladder (13 steps for Gemma, 15 for GaMS) on a fresh 300-item RefusEU-TRAIN body disjoint from all prior probes.\n\nFive artifact slots were planned. Slot~2 failed; the other four completed:\n\\begin{enumerate}\n  \\item Evaluation~3 (readout completion): paid-judge re-scoring.\n  \\item Experiment~13 (held-out confirmation, \\textbf{FAILED}): the container lost its GPU about 25 minutes in; no generation or primary label was produced.\n  \\item Experiment~14 (mechanism 2$\\times$3$\\times$3): input language $\\times$ output language $\\times$ dose.\n  \\item Experiment~15 (fine-grained lambda ladder): 13/15-step lambda curve on fresh 300-item body with random-direction controls.\n  \\item Research artifact: prior-art search and fact verification.\n\\end{enumerate}\n\nBecause slot~2 failed, iteration~4 has \\textbf{no held-out confirmation and no RQ2 result}.\n\n\\subsection{Artifact 15: Readout completion with paid judge (Evaluation~3)}\n%% workspace: gen_art_evaluation_3\n\nThis evaluation (gen\\_art\\_evaluation\\_3) applied the pre-registered paid readout to all saved edited and original rows from experiments~8, 9, 11 and the experiment~10 add-on block. The primary judge was gemini-2.5-flash. The second judge was gpt-4.1-mini on a stratified subset. Translate-then-judge (TTJ) applied NLLB SL-to-EN translation before judging. Blind adjudication used two Claude-family adjudicators (40-row overlap, inter-adjudicator kappa 0.69).\n\n\\subsubsection{Readout gate: FAILS}\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Readout gate (gemini-2.5-flash vs adjudication; iteration~4, evaluation~3).}\n\\label{tab:readout_gate}\n\\begin{tabular}{lcccc}\n\\toprule\nCell & Se [95\\% CI] & Sp [95\\% CI] & kappa gemini-gpt & Pass \\\\\n\\midrule\nGaMS-SL-edited & 0.91 [0.74, 0.97] & 0.73 [0.61, 0.83] & 0.39 & False \\\\\nGemma-SL-edited & 0.99 [0.87, 1.00] & 0.66 [0.43, 0.83] & 0.72 & False \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe paid judge has high sensitivity but specificity of 0.66--0.73 on edited Slovene rows (it over-calls REFUSE), below the pre-registered 0.80 floor. No readout tier passed the bake-off. All numbers below are estimates with their CIs, not primary verdicts.\n\n\\subsubsection{Pooled cross-model lag: sign confirmed, edit-induced component is zero}\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Pooled lag estimates (REML + HKSJ, $k = 3$ item bodies, R coding; iteration~4, evaluation~3).}\n\\label{tab:pooled_lag}\n\\begin{tabular}{lcccc}\n\\toprule\nReadout & $G_3$ [95\\% CI] & $G_{3,\\text{edit}}$ [95\\% CI] & IG [95\\% CI] & $I^2$ \\\\\n\\midrule\nRaw primary (gemini) & $-1.17$ [$-1.84$, $-0.50$] & 0.39 [$-1.95$, 2.74] & $-1.15$ [$-1.31$, $-0.99$] & 0.22 \\\\\nRG (unstable) & $-1.79$ [$-7.17$, 3.58] & n/a & $-2.02$ [$-5.40$, 1.35] & 0.00 \\\\\nPPI & $-1.77$ [$-1.89$, $-1.65$] & 0.20 [$-0.72$, 1.11] & $-2.00$ [$-3.19$, $-0.82$] & 0.00 \\\\\nTTJ & $-1.10$ [$-4.67$, 2.47] & 0.33 [$-6.52$, 7.18] & $-1.40$ [$-2.46$, $-0.33$] & 0.59 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe pooled lag is negative under every readout. The edit-induced component is centred near zero in every readout. Subtracting each model's own pre-edit language gap, the lag is entirely explained by the baseline offset: GaMS3 starts with less Slovene refusal than Gemma before any de-censoring. \\textbf{R-BASE (baseline offset) is the best-supported account.}\n\n\\subsubsection{Per-curve headlines}\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Per-curve $G_3$ decomposition (raw primary readout, R coding; iteration~4, evaluation~3).}\n\\label{tab:per_curve_g3}\n\\footnotesize\n\\begin{tabular}{lccccc}\n\\toprule\nCurve & $G_3$ [CI] & $G_{3,\\text{orig}}$ [CI] & $G_{3,\\text{edit}}$ [CI] & On support & Verdict \\\\\n\\midrule\nexp9 lambda & $-1.12$ [$-1.70$, $-0.63$] & $-2.56$ [$-4.07$, $-1.32$] & 1.43 [0.29, 2.98] & False & ESTIMATE \\\\\nexp11 FINAL & $-1.00$ [$-1.40$, $-0.68$] & $-1.11$ [$-2.74$, $-0.21$] & 0.10 [$-0.85$, 1.71] & True & CONFIRM-LAG \\\\\nexp8 A1 & $-1.54$ [$-2.11$, $-1.00$] & $-1.13$ [$-2.67$, 0.04] & $-0.41$ [$-1.65$, 1.26] & False & CONFIRM-LAG \\\\\nexp8 B & $-1.20$ [$-1.77$, $-0.58$] & $-1.33$ [$-2.37$, 0.78] & 0.12 [$-2.21$, 1.47] & True & ESTIMATE \\\\\nexp10 op point & $G_{3,\\text{op}}$ $-2.42$ [$-4.35$, $-1.53$] & 0.99 [$-1.10$, 3.53] & $-3.40$ [$-6.09$, $-1.30$] & -- & CONFIRM-LAG \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe pre-edit baseline ($G_{3,\\text{orig}}$) is strongly negative in every body, confirming the baseline offset. Nearest neighbours: Deng et al.\\ 2023 (instruction language), Upadhyaya and Sikdar 2026 (output language as outcome, not controlled factor).\n\nHeretic facts: Heretic @3521f86 is a 2.0.0.dev0 snapshot (2026-09-05). Croatian/Serbian/Bosnian make up 22.3\\% of base continued pretraining, a South-Slavic confound.\n\n\\subsection{Not executed or abandoned in iteration~4}\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Iteration-4 components not executed.}\n\\label{tab:not_executed_iter4}\n\\footnotesize\n\\begin{tabular}{llp{4cm}}\n\\toprule\nComponent & Status & Reason \\\\\n\\midrule\nexp13 Heretic edit \\& lambda grid & Not executed & GPU lost \\\\\nexp13 held-out confirmation (B-300) & Not executed & GPU lost \\\\\nexp13 random-dir.\\ controls & Not executed & GPU lost \\\\\nRQ2 natural RefusEU FINAL under edit & Not executed (owed since iter~1) & GPU lost \\\\\nexp13 substitute re-readout (19,195 rows) & Frozen, unlabelled & OpenRouter key limit \\\\\nexp13 judge tier gate & Ran; both tiers FAIL & Sp 0.27--0.55 \\\\\nexp14 harmful-content (ASR) readout & One cell only & Not completed \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n%% ================================================================\n\\section{Iteration 5}\n%% ================================================================\n\n\\subsection{Strategy}\n\nThree goals: (i)~confirm the C-OUT finding on a fresh 294-item body with a new Heretic edit, a suffix-free design, a full 2$\\times$3$\\times$3+controls matrix, and PPI correction (experiment~16); (ii)~run the deferred RefusEU FINAL evaluation with the full 1,300-item pool, random-edit and 256-token controls, and multiple readouts (experiment~17); (iii)~test the R-INCAP question---whether Gemma's Slovene reserve is real safety or production failure---with a StrongREJECT harmful-content endpoint alongside refusal (evaluation~4). Two support artifacts complete the iteration: a paper-number audit (evaluation~5) and a novelty and fact-check update (research~2).\n\n[Correction: C-LAG is now closed in favour of C-OUT. The overall cross-lingual abliteration lag is better characterised as an output-language effect (C-OUT) than as a generic cross-lingual lag (C-LAG).]\n\n[Correction: The novelty verdict for the main claim is downgraded from NOVEL to PARTIALLY OCCUPIED after \\citet{Addagada2026} and \\citet{Nguyen2026}.]\n\n\\subsection{Artifact 19: C-OUT confirmation (Experiment~16)}\n%% workspace: gen_art_experiment_16\n\nThis experiment (gen\\_art\\_experiment\\_16) tested whether the output-language effect (C-OUT)---edited Gemma refusing more when told to write in Slovene than in English---holds on a fresh 294-item body (146 StrongREJECT, 109 HarmBench, 39 JBB) with a new Heretic edit, using prediction-powered inference (PPI) as the primary estimator.\n\n\\subsubsection{Headline: C-OUT estimate}\n\nThe primary PPI estimate is OUT$_\\text{Gemma} = +2.43$ [$+0.89$, $+5.38$] log-odds: edited Gemma refuses 2.43 log-odds more when told to answer in Slovene than in English. The cross-model contrast dOUT $= -2.31$ [$-5.34$, $-0.68$] excludes zero. GaMS3 shows no output-language effect: OUT$_\\text{GaMS3} = +0.12$ [$-0.47$, $+0.72$], spanning zero. The input-language effect in Gemma is negative: IN$_\\text{Gemma} = -0.68$ [$-1.23$, $-0.36$]. Slovene input reduces refusal.\n\nAll confirmation clauses pass on the consensus reference, but the verdict is capped at ESTIMATE because the adjudication kappa on harmful content is 0.12 (gate requires 0.60).\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Primary-judge refusal rates on harmful items, selected cells ($n = 294$ per cell; iteration~5, experiment~16).}\n\\label{tab:cout_rates}\n\\footnotesize\n\\begin{tabular}{llcc}\n\\toprule\nModel & Cell & Dose & Refusal \\\\\n\\midrule\nGemma & EN$\\to$EN & hi & 0.330 \\\\\nGemma & EN$\\to$SL & lo & 0.884 \\\\\nGemma & EN$\\to$HU & lo & 0.731 \\\\\nGemma & SL$\\to$EN & lo & 0.344 \\\\\nGemma & SF\\_EN$\\to$EN & lo & 0.510 \\\\\nGemma & SF\\_SL$\\to$SL & lo & 0.827 \\\\\nGemma & EN$\\to$EN & zero & 0.918 \\\\\nGemma & EN$\\to$SL & zero & 0.969 \\\\\nGaMS3 & EN$\\to$EN & hi & 0.490 \\\\\nGaMS3 & EN$\\to$SL & hi & 0.449 \\\\\nGaMS3 & SF\\_EN$\\to$EN & hi & 0.527 \\\\\nGaMS3 & SF\\_SL$\\to$SL & hi & 0.616 \\\\\nGaMS3 & EN$\\to$EN & zero & 0.820 \\\\\nGaMS3 & EN$\\to$SL & zero & 0.786 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe suffix-free cells show the same pattern as the suffixed cells: Slovene output drives higher refusal in Gemma (0.827 vs 0.510 at low dose), ruling out a suffix artefact.\n\n\\subsubsection{SDT decomposition}\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Signal-detection DiD (Gemma minus GaMS3) at dose zero and dose$^*$ (iteration~5, experiment~16).}\n\\label{tab:sdt_exp16}\n\\begin{tabular}{llcc}\n\\toprule\nDose & Contrast & $d'$ DiD & $c$ DiD \\\\\n\\midrule\nzero & SL output & $-0.37$ [$-0.81$, 0.07] & $-0.65$ [$-0.90$, $-0.46$] \\\\\nlo & SL output & $+0.09$ [$-0.62$, 0.57] & $-1.07$ [$-1.42$, $-0.85$] \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe output-language effect sits in the criterion, not in discrimination. At the dose-matched lambda, the criterion DiD is $-1.07$ [$-1.42$, $-0.85$] and the $d'$ DiD is $+0.09$ [$-0.62$, 0.57], which includes zero.\n\n\\subsubsection{Judge validity}\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Judge error in decisive cells (LLM adjudication, NOT human; $n = 100$ per cell; iteration~5, experiment~16).}\n\\label{tab:judge_validity_exp16}\n\\footnotesize\n\\begin{tabular}{lcccc}\n\\toprule\nCell & Judge vs reference & Se & Sp & $n$ \\\\\n\\midrule\nGemma EN$\\to$EN & gemini\\_U vs adj\\_U & 0.93 & 0.63 & 99 \\\\\nGemma EN$\\to$SL & gemini\\_U vs adj\\_U & 1.00 & 0.94 & 99 \\\\\nGaMS3 EN$\\to$EN & gemini\\_U vs adj\\_U & 0.92 & 0.84 & 100 \\\\\nGaMS3 EN$\\to$SL & gemini\\_U vs adj\\_U & 1.00 & 0.82 & 99 \\\\\nGemma EN$\\to$EN & J1 vs adj\\_explicit & 1.00 & 0.46 & 100 \\\\\nGemma EN$\\to$SL & J1 vs adj\\_explicit & 1.00 & 0.35 & 100 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\subsubsection{Outcome}\n\n\\textbf{Verdict: ESTIMATE with WEAK anchor.} All confirmation clauses pass on the consensus reference. The verdict is capped at ESTIMATE because the harmful-content adjudication kappa is 0.12.\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n  \\centering\n  \\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig_cout_forest_v0.pdf}\n  \\caption{C-OUT confirmation forest plot. Edited Gemma's residual refusal follows the output language across item sources (iteration~5, experiment~16).}\n  \\label{fig:cout_forest}\n\\end{figure}\n\n\\subsection{Artifact 20: RefusEU FINAL (Experiment~17)}\n%% workspace: gen_art_experiment_17\n\nThis experiment (gen\\_art\\_experiment\\_17) measured what one English-only de-censoring edit buys on RefusEU's own 1,300 prompts per language, in both models and both languages. The judge stack used local substitutes (PolyGuard refusal, Qwen3Guard-Gen-8B, StrongREJECT fine-tuned evaluator). 11,600 rows were analysed across four conditions.\n\n\\subsubsection{The edit raises attack success in all four cells}\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Paired edit effects (orig $\\to$ edit@1.0, exact McNemar, Holm-corrected; iteration~5, experiment~17).}\n\\label{tab:refuseu_final}\n\\begin{tabular}{llcccl}\n\\toprule\nModel & Lang & ASR orig & ASR edit & Delta [95\\% CI] & Verdict \\\\\n\\midrule\nGemma & EN & 0.045 & 0.897 & 0.852 [0.831, 0.870] & ROBUST \\\\\nGemma & SL & 0.026 & 0.683 & 0.657 [0.629, 0.683] & ROBUST \\\\\nGaMS3 & EN & 0.033 & 0.970 & 0.937 [0.923, 0.949] & ROBUST \\\\\nGaMS3 & SL & 0.068 & 0.915 & 0.847 [0.826, 0.867] & ROBUST \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nAll four cells are ROBUST: the edit produces a massive increase in attack success on RefusEU prompts. The edit is more effective on GaMS3 than Gemma in both languages, and more effective in English than Slovene in both models.\n\n\\subsubsection{Language confound}\n\nThe English and Slovene prompt sets are different natural prompts with LaBSE similarity 0.55, so the SL-vs-EN difference within a model is \\textbf{not interpretable as a language effect}. Even in the high-similarity subset (LaBSE $\\geq 0.70$, $n = 58$), the SL-EN gap in Gemma is $-0.190$ [$-0.345$, $-0.035$] and in GaMS3 is $-0.035$ [$-0.121$, 0.052].\n\n\\subsubsection{Corrected ASR}\n\nRogan-Gladen corrected deltas (using per-cell Se/Sp from blind author-model adjudication on 60 rows per cell): Gemma EN $\\delta_\\text{RG} = 0.863$ [0.811, 0.892]; Gemma SL $\\delta_\\text{RG} = 0.578$ [0.473, 0.639]; GaMS3 EN $\\delta_\\text{RG} = 0.967$ [0.927, 0.976]; GaMS3 SL $\\delta_\\text{RG} = 0.884$ [0.826, 0.912].\n\n\\subsubsection{Ranking vs thresholding}\n\nAUROC is high in all cells (0.887--1.000), meaning the guards rank harmful above harmless correctly. The failure is in the shipped decision threshold, not in the underlying score. This is consistent with \\citeauthor{Aziz2026}'s~\\citeyearpar{Aziz2026} calibration-not-representation account.\n\n\\subsubsection{Verdict}\n\nAll four paired-edit cells are ROBUST. The edit is effective on RefusEU prompts. The StrongREJECT fine-tuned evaluator has near-zero sensitivity for Gemma, confirming it cannot substitute for a paid rubric judge on this model.\n\n\\subsection{Artifact 21: R-INCAP safety evaluation (Evaluation~4)}\n%% workspace: gen_art_evaluation_4\n\nThis artifact (gen\\_art\\_evaluation\\_4) tested whether Gemma's Slovene-output reserve is real safety (harmful content separates) or production failure. It re-used experiment~14's body (200 items per cell) with refusal and StrongREJECT harmful-content measurements.\n\n\\subsubsection{Harmful content separates (reserve = safety)}\n\n\\textbf{At high dose:} the output-language refusal contrast is OUT$_\\text{R} = 2.67$ [2.29, 3.12] log-odds and the harmful-content contrast is OUT$_\\text{U} = 2.61$ [2.20, 3.07]. Both are positive and exclude zero. Gemma refuses more in Slovene \\textbf{and} produces less harmful content in Slovene. The PPI-corrected refusal is even larger: OUT$_\\text{R}$(PPI explicit) $= 5.39$ [4.91, 5.85].\n\n\\textbf{At low dose:} the same pattern holds: OUT$_\\text{R} = 2.05$ [1.61, 2.65] and OUT$_\\text{U} = 2.80$ [2.25, 3.69].\n\n\\textbf{Verdict: R-INCAP = HARMFUL CONTENT SEPARATES (reserve = safety).} The reserve is not a production failure. File: /ai-inventor/aii_data/runs/run_2MI56L8wzgdI/4_gen_paper_repo/_4_assemble_paper/report_workspace/exec_summary.tex

\documentclass[11pt,letterpaper]{article}
\usepackage{graphicx, geometry, amsmath, hyperref, url, booktabs, xcolor, array, enumitem}
\geometry{margin=1in}
\hypersetup{colorlinks=true, linkcolor=black, citecolor=black, urlcolor=black}
\setlength{\parskip}{4pt plus 1pt minus 1pt}
\setlength{\parindent}{0pt}

\title{Executive Summary\\[4pt]
  \large Why Slovene Refusal Outlasts English Abliteration}
\author{Internal Research Report --- September 2026}
\date{}

\begin{document}
\maketitle
\thispagestyle{empty}

\section*{Goal}

GaMS3-12B-Instruct and Gemma-3-12B-IT share a pretrained ancestor (gemma-3-12b-pt) but diverge in safety supervision language: GaMS3 received Slovene continued pretraining and supervised fine-tuning with ${\sim}7{,}000$ safety-refusal examples drawn from machine-translated Qwen-family responses, while Gemma-IT received Google's standard multilingual post-training. Five iterations of experiments (23 artifacts total) tested whether Slovene-taught refusal transfers to English, whether English-only abliteration (Heretic) removes Slovene refusal equally in both models, and what mechanism explains any residual Slovene refusal.

\section*{Headline Findings}

\begin{table}[!htbp]
\centering
\footnotesize
\begin{tabular}{p{3.5cm}lp{5cm}l}
\toprule
Finding & Source & Key number & Grade \\
\midrule
Criterion shift (original models, HARD set) & Exp.~5 (iter.~2) & $c$ DiD $= +0.52$ [0.39, 0.67]; $d'$ DiD $\approx 0$ & ESTIMATE \\[2pt]
C-OUT: output language drives residual refusal & Exp.~16 (iter.~5) & OUT$_\text{Gemma}$(PPI) $= +2.43$ [$+0.89$, $+5.38$]; dOUT $= -2.31$ [$-5.34$, $-0.68$] & ESTIMATE (WEAK) \\[2pt]
R-BASE: lag is baseline, not edit-induced & Exp.~15 (iter.~4) & $G_{3,\text{edit}} = +0.47$ [$-0.96$, 2.14]; slopes $\approx 1$ & ESTIMATE \\[2pt]
Identity anchoring & Exp.~5 (iter.~2) & FINAL DiD$_\text{id} = 3.46$ [2.55, 4.62] & PASS \\[2pt]
Edit effective on RefusEU FINAL & Exp.~17 (iter.~5) & All 4 cells ROBUST ($n = 1{,}300$ per cell) & ROBUST \\[2pt]
Utility: no SL damage & Exp.~12 (iter.~3) & All $H < 0.05$; excess asymmetry $+0.051$ [0.012, 0.093] & OK \\[2pt]
R-INCAP: reserve is real safety & Eval.~4 (iter.~5) & Harmful-content OUT $= 2.61$ [2.20, 3.07] at hi dose & ESTIMATE (WEAK) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\textbf{Criterion shift on original models.} Gemma over-refuses benign Slovene prompts (false-alarm rate 0.569 vs 0.364 in English), while GaMS3 is language-invariant (0.273 in both). The DiD in discrimination $d'$ is near zero ($-0.003$); the DiD in criterion $c$ is $+0.52$ [0.38, 0.68]. This replicates across experiments~5, 9, 14, and~16 on original models. On edited models the criterion-shift difference disappears (DiD$_c = 0.14$ [$-0.78$, 1.12]).

\textbf{Output-language effect (C-OUT).} Experiment~16 replicated on a fresh 294-item body with prediction-powered inference correction: edited Gemma refuses 2.43 log-odds more when told to answer in Slovene than in English. GaMS3 shows no output-language effect (OUT$_\text{GaMS3} = +0.12$ [$-0.47$, $+0.72$]). The input-language effect is negative in Gemma ($-0.68$ [$-1.23$, $-0.36$]): Slovene input reduces refusal. The signal-detection decomposition places the effect in the criterion, not discrimination.

\textbf{The lag is baseline (R-BASE).} The cross-lingual abliteration lag is better characterised as a pre-edit model difference than an edit-induced effect. On experiment~15's fine-grained lambda ladder (MDE 0.42, the study's most powerful estimate), the edit-induced component is $+0.47$ [$-0.96$, 2.14] and both models' curves run parallel with slopes near 1. In every item body, the pre-edit baseline $G_{3,\text{orig}}$ is negative.

\textbf{Reserve is safety, not production failure.} Gemma's Slovene-output reserve produces less harmful content, not just more refusal: the harmful-content output-language contrast is 2.61 [2.20, 3.07] at high dose. The four-class decomposition shows half of the non-compliance is deflection (production-failure index difference 0.46 [0.23, 0.65]), consistent with the relevance curse.

\section*{Dead Ends}

\begin{table}[!htbp]
\centering
\footnotesize
\begin{tabular}{p{4.2cm}p{8.5cm}}
\toprule
Hypothesis & What killed it \\
\midrule
Alt.~2: base-checkpoint geometry & delta-$d'$ sign depends on layer; base geometry explains 4.2\% of refusal variance \\
Alt.~3: persona gating & Manipulation check failed; premise (Slovene surplus) contradicted by the data \\
Alt.~4: prefill-depth signature & No readout can validly score prefill continuations (kappa $\leq 0.21$) \\
Ancestor-direction induction & Pretrained direction never reached refusal rate 0.50 in any cell \\
Geometry hypothesis (M-a) & EN/SL directions nearly collinear at own $L^*$ ($\cos \geq 0.986$); result is layer-dependent \\
Induction hypothesis (M-b) & Slovene-perpendicular component inert as refusal inducer ($\alpha_{50}$ right-censored) \\
Dose contrast (main vs alt.~1) & Underpowered across all 5 iterations; MDE exceeds $2m$ on every readout \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\section*{What the Edit Does on RefusEU}

On the full 1,300-item RefusEU FINAL reserved split (experiment~17), the Heretic edit at $\lambda = 1.0$ is effective in all four model$\times$language cells:

\begin{table}[!htbp]
\centering
\footnotesize
\begin{tabular}{llccl}
\toprule
Model & Language & ASR orig & ASR edit & Verdict \\
\midrule
Gemma & EN & 0.045 & 0.897 & ROBUST \\
Gemma & SL & 0.026 & 0.683 & ROBUST \\
GaMS3 & EN & 0.033 & 0.970 & ROBUST \\
GaMS3 & SL & 0.068 & 0.915 & ROBUST \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

The edit is more effective on GaMS3 than Gemma in both languages. The English and Slovene prompt sets are different (LaBSE similarity 0.55), so within-model SL-vs-EN differences are not a pure language effect.

\section*{Utility Control}

The English-only abliteration edit does not damage Slovene downstream skills more than English ones. All macro headroom-normalised losses are below 0.05. Language asymmetry $A = H_\text{SL} - H_\text{EN}$ is positive (Slovene hurt less) in every cell. Random-adjusted excess asymmetry excludes zero for GaMS3 ($+0.051$ [$+0.012$, $+0.093$]). Localised costs: GaMS3 English ARC-Challenge ($-3.7$\,pp, $p = 0.041$) and BoolQ ($-2.0$/$-2.3$\,pp). Belebele comprehension and FLORES fluency are unaffected.

\section*{Evidence Quality Limitations}

\begin{itemize}[nosep, leftmargin=*]
  \item \textbf{The readout gate has never passed.} Every LLM judge has kappa at most 0.43 on edited rows against blind adjudication; the paid gemini frontier judge has specificity 0.66--0.73 (over-calls REFUSE). All blind adjudication is author-LLM, not human.
  \item \textbf{The frozen-core Heretic procedure} (bf16, 80 trials, Heretic's selection rule) has never been run. Every edit is an iteration-1 reduced-trial NF4 fallback.
  \item \textbf{Natural RefusEU reserved-split prompts} have never been scored under the edit (experiment~17 used the PolyGuard readout, not the pre-registered gemini judge).
  \item \textbf{R-BASE baseline is fragile} in most item bodies: experiment~15's fragility index is 1 (one Gemma SL flip at $\lambda = 0$ moves the baseline inside the margin). Only experiment~9 has a robust offset (fragility index 9).
  \item \textbf{The harmful-content adjudicator kappa} is 0.12 in experiment~16 (gate requires 0.60), traced to truncation handling. Refusal kappa is 0.90.
  \item \textbf{GaMS3 failed the output-language manipulation} off the English-input row (SL$\to$EN compliance 0.00 in experiment~14), so the input-vs-output decomposition is unavailable for GaMS3.
\end{itemize}

\section*{Novelty}

The main claim is \textbf{PARTIALLY OCCUPIED} (downgraded from NOVEL). Two preprints partly occupy the lane: Addagada (2609.08373) forces the output language and finds a relevance curse; Nguyen et al.\ (2608.26186) cross prompt and response language on benign content. The narrowed design---crossing both factors with safety endpoints, a sibling pair sharing a pretrained ancestor, partial-dose edit plus a public checkpoint, Hungarian as a third language, and a constant suffix in all cells---remains unoccupied as of September 2026 (medium-low confidence).

\section*{Open Items for Future Work}

\begin{enumerate}[nosep, leftmargin=*]
  \item C-OUT deserves pre-registered confirmation with a validated readout and human adjudication on edited rows.
  \item If R-BASE is correct, the lag is an artefact of model selection (GaMS3 was trained to refuse less in Slovene), not a property of the abliteration procedure.
  \item The dose contrast (main claim vs alternate~1) remains underpowered across all five iterations; a larger item body or a different operationalisation of ``dose'' may be needed.
  \item The M-OUT production-fluency account (refusal as a fallback when the model must produce harmful content in a language it generates poorly) was hypothesised but never directly tested.
\end{enumerate}

\vfill
\noindent\rule{\textwidth}{0.4pt}
\footnotesize
Full report: 47 pages, 5 iterations, 23 artifacts, 32 tables, 7 figures. Spend: approximately \$25. All code and data artifacts are at \texttt{github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-2cf2a7-does-slovene-taught-refusal-survive}.

\end{document}

On edited models the criterion-shift difference disappears (DiD$_c = 0.14$ [$-0.78$, 1.12]).\n\n\\textbf{Output-language effect (C-OUT).} Experiment~16 replicated on a fresh 294-item body with prediction-powered inference correction: edited Gemma refuses 2.43 log-odds more when told to answer in Slovene than in English. GaMS3 shows no output-language effect (OUT$_\\text{GaMS3} = +0.12$ [$-0.47$, $+0.72$]). The input-language effect is negative in Gemma ($-0.68$ [$-1.23$, $-0.36$]): Slovene input reduces refusal. The signal-detection decomposition places the effect in the criterion, not discrimination.\n\n\\textbf{The lag is baseline (R-BASE).} The cross-lingual abliteration lag is better characterised as a pre-edit model difference than an edit-induced effect. On experiment~15's fine-grained lambda ladder (MDE 0.42, the study's most powerful estimate), the edit-induced component is $+0.47$ [$-0.96$, 2.14] and both models' curves run parallel with slopes near 1. In every item body, the pre-edit baseline $G_{3,\\text{orig}}$ is negative.\n\n\\textbf{Reserve is safety, not production failure.} Gemma's Slovene-output reserve produces less harmful content, not just more refusal: the harmful-content output-language contrast is 2.61 [2.20, 3.07] at high dose. The four-class decomposition shows half of the non-compliance is deflection (production-failure index difference 0.46 [0.23, 0.65]), consistent with the relevance curse.\n\n\\section*{Dead Ends}\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\footnotesize\n\\begin{tabular}{p{4.2cm}p{8.5cm}}\n\\toprule\nHypothesis & What killed it \\\\\n\\midrule\nAlt.~2: base-checkpoint geometry & delta-$d'$ sign depends on layer; base geometry explains 4.2\\% of refusal variance \\\\\nAlt.~3: persona gating & Manipulation check failed; premise (Slovene surplus) contradicted by the data \\\\\nAlt.~4: prefill-depth signature & No readout can validly score prefill continuations (kappa $\\leq 0.21$) \\\\\nAncestor-direction induction & Pretrained direction never reached refusal rate 0.50 in any cell \\\\\nGeometry hypothesis (M-a) & EN/SL directions nearly collinear at own $L^*$ ($\\cos \\geq 0.986$); result is layer-dependent \\\\\nInduction hypothesis (M-b) & Slovene-perpendicular component inert as refusal inducer ($\\alpha_{50}$ right-censored) \\\\\nDose contrast (main vs alt.~1) & Underpowered across all 5 iterations; MDE exceeds $2m$ on every readout \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\section*{What the Edit Does on RefusEU}\n\nOn the full 1,300-item RefusEU FINAL reserved split (experiment~17), the Heretic edit at $\\lambda = 1.0$ is effective in all four model$\\times$language cells:\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\footnotesize\n\\begin{tabular}{llccl}\n\\toprule\nModel & Language & ASR orig & ASR edit & Verdict \\\\\n\\midrule\nGemma & EN & 0.045 & 0.897 & ROBUST \\\\\nGemma & SL & 0.026 & 0.683 & ROBUST \\\\\nGaMS3 & EN & 0.033 & 0.970 & ROBUST \\\\\nGaMS3 & SL & 0.068 & 0.915 & ROBUST \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe edit is more effective on GaMS3 than Gemma in both languages. The English and Slovene prompt sets are different (LaBSE similarity 0.55), so within-model SL-vs-EN differences are not a pure language effect.\n\n\\section*{Utility Control}\n\nThe English-only abliteration edit does not damage Slovene downstream skills more than English ones. All macro headroom-normalised losses are below 0.05. Language asymmetry $A = H_\\text{SL} - H_\\text{EN}$ is positive (Slovene hurt less) in every cell. Random-adjusted excess asymmetry excludes zero for GaMS3 ($+0.051$ [$+0.012$, $+0.093$]). Localised costs: GaMS3 English ARC-Challenge ($-3.7$\\,pp, $p = 0.041$) and BoolQ ($-2.0$/$-2.3$\\,pp). Belebele comprehension and FLORES fluency are unaffected.\n\n\\section*{Evidence Quality Limitations}\n\n\\begin{itemize}[nosep, leftmargin=*]\n  \\item \\textbf{The readout gate has never passed.} Every LLM judge has kappa at most 0.43 on edited rows against blind adjudication; the paid gemini frontier judge has specificity 0.66--0.73 (over-calls REFUSE). All blind adjudication is author-LLM, not human.\n  \\item \\textbf{The frozen-core Heretic procedure} (bf16, 80 trials, Heretic's selection rule) has never been run. Every edit is an iteration-1 reduced-trial NF4 fallback.\n  \\item \\textbf{Natural RefusEU reserved-split prompts} have never been scored under the edit (experiment~17 used the PolyGuard readout, not the pre-registered gemini judge).\n  \\item \\textbf{R-BASE baseline is fragile} in most item bodies: experiment~15's fragility index is 1 (one Gemma SL flip at $\\lambda = 0$ moves the baseline inside the margin). Only experiment~9 has a robust offset (fragility index 9).\n  \\item \\textbf{The harmful-content adjudicator kappa} is 0.12 in experiment~16 (gate requires 0.60), traced to truncation handling. Refusal kappa is 0.90.\n  \\item \\textbf{GaMS3 failed the output-language manipulation} off the English-input row (SL$\\to$EN compliance 0.00 in experiment~14), so the input-vs-output decomposition is unavailable for GaMS3.\n\\end{itemize}\n\n\\section*{Novelty}\n\nThe main claim is \\textbf{PARTIALLY OCCUPIED} (downgraded from NOVEL). Two preprints partly occupy the lane: Addagada (2609.08373) forces the output language and finds a relevance curse; Nguyen et al.\\ (2608.26186) cross prompt and response language on benign content. The narrowed design---crossing both factors with safety endpoints, a sibling pair sharing a pretrained ancestor, partial-dose edit plus a public checkpoint, Hungarian as a third language, and a constant suffix in all cells---remains unoccupied as of September 2026 (medium-low confidence).\n\n\\section*{Open Items for Future Work}\n\n\\begin{enumerate}[nosep, leftmargin=*]\n  \\item C-OUT deserves pre-registered confirmation with a validated readout and human adjudication on edited rows.\n  \\item If R-BASE is correct, the lag is an artefact of model selection (GaMS3 was trained to refuse less in Slovene), not a property of the abliteration procedure.\n  \\item The dose contrast (main claim vs alternate~1) remains underpowered across all five iterations; a larger item body or a different operationalisation of ``dose'' may be needed.\n  \\item The M-OUT production-fluency account (refusal as a fallback when the model must produce harmful content in a language it generates poorly) was hypothesised but never directly tested.\n\\end{enumerate}\n\n\\vfill\n\\noindent\\rule{\\textwidth}{0.4pt}\n\\footnotesize\nFull report: 47 pages, 5 iterations, 23 artifacts, 32 tables, 7 figures. Spend: approximately \\$25. Evidence grade: ESTIMATE across iterations; the readout gate has never passed (all adjudication is author-LLM, not human).\n\nA secondary finding is the output-language effect (C-OUT): edited Gemma refuses 2.43 log-odds more when told to answer in Slovene than in English (PPI-corrected estimate from experiment~16, iteration~5: OUT$_\\text{Gemma} = +2.43$ [$+0.89$, $+5.38$]).  The C-OUT verdict is ESTIMATE with WEAK anchor: all confirmation clauses pass on the consensus reference, but the harmful-content adjudication kappa is 0.12 (gate requires 0.60).\n\nThe full report is 47 pages.\n\n\\section{Goal}\n\nThis run investigated whether Slovene-taught refusal in GaMS3-12B-Instruct transfers to English and whether an English-only de-censoring tool (Heretic) can strip bilingual refusal as readily as monolingual refusal.  GaMS3 and Gemma-3-12B-IT share a pretrained ancestor (gemma-3-12b-pt) but diverge in their post-training: GaMS3 received Slovene continued pretraining on 140 billion tokens and supervised fine-tuning with approximately 7,000 safety-refusal examples drawn largely from machine-translated Qwen-family responses, while Gemma-IT received Google's standard multilingual post-training.  The run tested a main claim (behaviour-level reach: refusal transfers to English at every hazard-category grain), four pre-registered alternates, and two mechanistic hypotheses, across five iterations totalling 23 artifacts.\n\n\\section{What Was Tried}\n\n\\textbf{Iteration~1} (5~artifacts): screened the main claim and four alternates on SCORE items.  Measured refusal difference-in-differences, dose contrast, base-checkpoint geometry, persona gating, and Heretic abliteration transfer curves.\n\n\\textbf{Iteration~2} (5~artifacts): ran the pre-registered FINAL evaluation on the reserved RefusEU split, tested teacher-inheritance from the Qwen family, re-tested the Heretic transfer curve on a fresh 200-item probe, and reconciled all iteration-1 findings onto a single readout.\n\n\\textbf{Iteration~3} (5~artifacts): repaired the experiment~8 readout with validated judges, confirmed the cross-lingual abliteration lag on a fresh 300-item probe with a DeBERTa judge, tested the geometry and induction mechanistic hypotheses, ran the reserved-split FINAL with Hungarian, and ran a utility control on six downstream tasks.\n\n\\textbf{Iteration~4} (4~artifacts + 1~failed): completed the readout with paid frontier judges, tested the input-language vs output-language mechanism in a 2$\\times$3$\\times$3 design, ran a fine-grained 13/15-step lambda ladder on a fresh 300-item body, and conducted a prior-art search.  The held-out confirmation (experiment~13) failed when the container lost its GPU.\n\n\\textbf{Iteration~5} (5~artifacts): confirmed the output-language effect (C-OUT) on a fresh 294-item body with PPI correction, ran RefusEU FINAL on 1,300 prompts per language with attack-success measurement, tested whether Gemma's Slovene reserve is real safety or production failure, and audited all paper numbers.\n\n\\section{Key Results}\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\footnotesize\n\\begin{tabular}{p{3.8cm}lp{4.8cm}l}\n\\toprule\nFinding & Source & Number & Grade \\\\\n\\midrule\nCriterion shift (original, HARD) & Exp.~5 (iter.~2) & $c$ DiD $= +0.52$ [0.39, 0.67]; $d'$ DiD $\\approx 0$ & ESTIMATE \\\\\nC-OUT: output lang.\\ drives residual refusal & Exp.~16 (iter.~5) & OUT$_\\text{Gemma}$(PPI) $= +2.43$ [$+0.89$, $+5.38$] & ESTIMATE (WEAK) \\\\\nR-BASE: lag is pre-edit & Exp.~15 (iter.~4) & $G_{3,\\text{edit}} = +0.47$ [$-0.96$, 2.14]; slopes $\\approx 1$ & ESTIMATE \\\\\nIdentity anchoring & Exp.~5 (iter.~2) & FINAL identity DiD $= 3.46$ [2.55, 4.62] & PASS \\\\\nEdit effective on RefusEU FINAL & Exp.~17 (iter.~5) & All 4 paired-edit cells ROBUST & ROBUST \\\\\nUtility: no SL damage & Exp.~12 (iter.~3) & All $H < 0.05$; SL spared vs random & OK \\\\\nR-INCAP: reserve is safety & Eval.~4 (iter.~5) & Harmful content separates at both doses & ESTIMATE (WEAK) \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\section{What Failed}\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\footnotesize\n\\begin{tabular}{p{4cm}p{8.5cm}}\n\\toprule\nDead end & Reason \\\\\n\\midrule\nAlternate~2 (base geometry) & delta-$d'$ sign depends on layer; layer-dependent at common layer \\\\\nInduction hypothesis & Slovene-perpendicular direction inert as refusal inducer \\\\\nExperiment~13 (held-out confirm.) & GPU lost after 25 minutes; no output produced \\\\\nDose contrast (main vs alt.~1) & Underpowered across all 5 iterations; # Bilingual Refusal Suppression Report

Internal research report documenting five iterations of experiments on bilingual refusal in GaMS3-12B-Instruct vs Gemma-3-12B-IT.

## Layout

| Path | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `report.tex` | LaTeX source for the full 47-page chronological research report |
| `report.pdf` | Compiled report |
| `exec_summary.tex` | LaTeX source for the 4-page executive summary |
| `exec_summary.pdf` | Compiled executive summary |
| `references.bib` | BibTeX bibliography (37 entries) |
| `figures/` | Seven pre-rendered vector PDF figures included in the report |
| `.aii/manifest.yaml` | Storage manifest for heavy files |

## Figures

Seven figures are included from the experiment artifacts:

- `fig_forest_did_v0.pdf` — Category-level difference-in-differences forest plot
- `fig_transfer_curve_v0.pdf` — Slovene-vs-English refusal transfer curve
- `fig_hard_sdt_v0.pdf` — Signal-detection decomposition on HARD items
- `fig_transfer_retest_v0.pdf` — Transfer curve re-test on fresh probe
- `fig_lambda_exp9_v0.pdf` — Lambda curve on fresh 300-item probe
- `fig_lambda_ladder_v0.pdf` — Fine-grained lambda ladder
- `fig_cout_forest_v0.pdf` — C-OUT confirmation forest plot

Two figures referenced in the draft text had no available files (`fig_mechanism_2x3`, `fig_rincap_composition`) and are omitted.

## Building

Requires a LaTeX distribution with pdflatex and bibtex.

```bash
pdflatex -interaction=nonstopmode report.tex
bibtex report
pdflatex -interaction=nonstopmode report.tex
pdflatex -interaction=nonstopmode report.tex

pdflatex -interaction=nonstopmode exec_summary.tex
pdflatex -interaction=nonstopmode exec_summary.tex
```

On systems where `bibtex` is aliased (e.g. Debian), use `bibtex.original report` instead.

## Restoring removed files

No files are marked for deletion. All workspace content is kept.
